title: Fix Canvas renderer IR indexing
description: Bugfix: fm-render-canvas Canvas2dRenderer currently indexes into ir.nodes/ir.edges by enumeration index of layout.nodes/layout.edges. This is incorrect because layout ordering can diverge from IR ordering, and layout can filter out unresolved edges. Fix crates/fm-render-canvas/src/renderer.rs to use LayoutNodeBox.node_index and LayoutEdgePath.edge_index consistently when looking up IR nodes/edges and emitting IDs/labels/styles. Add regression test if feasible. Quality gates must pass (fmt/check/clippy/tests).
close_reason: Canvas renderer now uses stable layout->IR indices for nodes/edges; gates pass.

title: Fix Canvas auto-fit padding/centering
description: Bugfix: fm-render-canvas Canvas2dRenderer currently applies padding twice when auto_fit is enabled: fit_to_viewport() already accounts for screen-space padding and centering, but renderer also shifts all diagram coordinates by config.padding (diagram-space), causing mis-centering and asymmetric margins (especially when zoom != 1). Fix renderer offset math so auto_fit uses offset = -layout.bounds.(x,y) (normalize only), while non-auto-fit can still apply padding as diagram-space translation. Add regression tests using MockCanvas2dContext operations to ensure auto_fit does not add padding to rect coordinates.
close_reason: Canvas auto-fit padding/centering fixed; viewport clamped; regression tests added; gates pass.

title: Emit cached minified flowchart CSS directly

title: Implement specialized sequence diagram layout and rendering
description:
Sequence diagrams need a completely different layout approach from graph diagrams. Implement a dedicated sequence diagram pipeline:

Layout: (1) Participants arranged horizontally with equal spacing (or auto-sized by name length). (2) Lifelines as vertical dashed lines extending downward. (3) Messages as horizontal arrows between lifelines, stacked vertically in order. (4) Activation boxes showing active periods. (5) Combined fragments (alt, opt, loop, par, break, critical) as labeled rectangles spanning lifelines. (6) Notes attached to lifelines or spanning between them. (7) Self-messages as loops returning to same lifeline.

This does NOT use the Sugiyama layout -- it is a sequential vertical stacking algorithm. Must handle: actor vs participant distinction, message numbering (autonumber), parallel fragment support, nested fragments, message arrowhead types (solid, dashed, open, cross).

Depends on: fm-core, fm-parser (sequence diagram parsing).

title: Create E2E test script with full pipeline validation and detailed logging
description:
Create scripts/e2e_test.sh (modeled on DCG's e2e_test.sh) that exercises the complete FrankenMermaid pipeline end-to-end. The script must:

1. TEST CORPUS: Ship a tests/e2e_corpus/ directory with .mmd files covering every diagram type. At least 3 files per type: simple, complex, edge-case. Include malformed inputs for error recovery testing.

2. PER-FILE TEST PIPELINE: For each .mmd file:
   a. Run fm-cli render --format svg -- verify exit code 0, SVG output is non-empty and valid XML
   b. Run fm-cli render --format term -- verify exit code 0, output contains box-drawing characters
   c. Run fm-cli parse --format json -- verify exit code 0, JSON output parses, has nodes array
   d. Run fm-cli detect -- verify exit code 0, detected type matches expected type
   e. If golden SVG exists in tests/e2e_golden/, compare output hash

3. ERROR RECOVERY TESTS: For each malformed input:
   a. Verify fm-cli does NOT exit with error (exit 0)
   b. Verify output contains diagnostic warnings
   c. Verify SVG output is still produced (best-effort)

4. PERFORMANCE BUDGET: Time each render. Report median/p95/max. Fail if any single render exceeds 5 seconds.

5. DETAILED LOGGING: Every test case prints:
   - Input file name and size
   - Detected diagram type and confidence
   - Node count, edge count, cluster count
   - SVG output size (bytes)
   - Render time (ms)
   - PASS/FAIL status with specific reason on failure
   At end: summary table with pass/fail counts per diagram type.

6. OUTPUT: JSON report in e2e_output.json with all test results. Exit code 0 if all pass, 1 if any fail.

7. CI INTEGRATION: --ci flag for machine-readable output. --verbose flag for debug-level logging. --filter flag to run subset of tests.

Target: 100+ individual test cases across all diagram types.

title: Spectral Graph Partitioning for Hierarchical Layout Decomposition
description:
## Spectral Graph Partitioning for Hierarchical Layout Decomposition

Use spectral graph partitioning (eigendecomposition of the graph Laplacian) to decompose large diagrams into well-separated subgraphs for hierarchical layout, enabling divide-and-conquer layout strategies that scale to thousands of nodes.

## Mathematical Foundation
The graph Laplacian L = D - A (degree matrix minus adjacency matrix) encodes the graph's connectivity structure. Its eigenvalues and eigenvectors reveal graph structure:
- λ_1 = 0 always (constant eigenvector)
- λ_2 (Fiedler value) = algebraic connectivity; its eigenvector (Fiedler vector) provides the optimal bisection
- λ_k reveals k-way partition quality

**Spectral bisection algorithm:**
1. Compute Fiedler vector v_2 (eigenvector of second-smallest eigenvalue of L)
2. Partition nodes: S_1 = {i : v_2[i] < median(v_2)}, S_2 = {i : v_2[i] >= median(v_2)}
3. This minimizes the normalized cut: NCut(S_1, S_2) = cut(S_1, S_2) * (1/vol(S_1) + 1/vol(S_2))
4. Recursively bisect for k-way partitioning

**For diagram layout:**
- Partition large diagram into 4-8 clusters
- Layout each cluster independently (parallel execution possible)
- Stitch clusters together using inter-cluster edge routing
- Result: O(n/k) layout per partition instead of O(n), with inter-cluster overhead

**Eigensolver choice:**
- For n < 500: dense eigendecomposition (O(n³))
- For n >= 500: Lanczos iteration (O(n*k*iter), typically iter < 100)
- Rust crate: nalgebra (dense) or sprs + arpack-like (sparse Lanczos)

## Key Papers
- Fiedler, "Algebraic Connectivity of Graphs" (Czech Math Journal 1973)
- Shi & Malik, "Normalized Cuts and Image Segmentation" (IEEE TPAMI 2000) — NCut
- Von Luxburg, "A Tutorial on Spectral Clustering" (Statistics and Computing 2007)
- Koren, "Drawing Graphs by Eigenvectors" (Computers & Mathematics 2005) — spectral layout

## Implementation in FrankenMermaid
1. Add `nalgebra` crate for eigendecomposition (already likely a transitive dependency).
2. Implement `SpectralPartitioner` that takes a graph and returns k partitions.
3. Compute Fiedler vector via Lanczos iteration for sparse graphs.
4. Implement recursive bisection for k-way partitioning.
5. Integrate with layout pipeline: for graphs > threshold (e.g., 200 nodes), spectral partition first, then layout each partition.
6. Implement inter-cluster edge routing (edges crossing partition boundaries).
7. Benchmark: layout time for 1000, 5000, 10000 node graphs with/without partitioning.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Spectral bisection produces balanced partitions (each partition within 40-60% of total)
- [ ] Fiedler vector computed correctly (verified against known graph spectra)
- [ ] Layout quality of partitioned approach within 10% of monolithic layout
- [ ] Layout time improvement >= 3x for 5000+ node graphs
- [ ] Inter-cluster edges routed without visual artifacts
- [ ] Threshold tuning: spectral partitioning skipped for small graphs (< 200 nodes)
- [ ] Decision contract: adopt if speedup >= 2x AND quality within 15%
close_reason: Implemented spectral graph partitioning module (crates/fm-layout/src/spectral.rs) with: Laplacian construction from IR edges, Fiedler vector computation via nalgebra eigendecomposition, spectral bisection with balance constraints, recursive k-way partitioning, partition mapping for layout pipeline integration, threshold-based activation, normalized cut quality metric. 16 unit tests covering Laplacian properties, Fiedler vector correctness, barbell/clique/star/complete/path graph partitioning, balance constraints, partition mapping roundtrip, and quality metrics. All quality gates pass (check, clippy, fmt).

title: CgaRect::is_valid accepts rects whose edges overflow CgaLineSegment::closest_point
description:
CgaRect::is_valid checks that x + width and y + height stay finite, but NOT that an edge's squared length stays finite. CgaLineSegment::closest_point rejects len_sq = dx*dx + dy*dy when it overflows to +inf.

So there is a band of rects that is_valid ACCEPTS but every edge query fails closed on:

  CgaRect::new(0.0, 0.0, f64::MAX, f64::MAX)   // is_valid() == true
  .closest_boundary_point(&CgaPoint::new(1.0, 2.0)) == CgaPoint::origin()

i.e. a rect the type says is well-formed silently degrades to the origin sentinel, indistinguishable from a rejected malformed rect. Callers cannot tell 'no answer' from 'the answer is (0,0)'.

Found while resolving bd-r3fw (rect closest-boundary oracle divergence). NOT a live defect for the engine: layout coordinates are bounded far below sqrt(f64::MAX) ~ 1.3e154, and the 1e150 negative control in rect_closest_boundary_matches_sqrt_reference shows the guarantee still holds across the entire realistic range. Pinned by an explicit assertion in that test so a change to either side is not silent.

Decide deliberately, do not paper over: either (a) tighten is_valid to reject edges whose squared length overflows, so is_valid and closest_point agree on one domain, or (b) keep the split and document that origin is a sentinel, not a coordinate. Option (a) is the fail-closed-consistent choice; it narrows an accepted domain, so it needs the existing 1e150 control plus a check of every is_valid caller.
close_reason:
Fixed in c69034f6. ROOT CAUSE was NOT CgaRect::is_valid (the bead's own framing): the defect is in CgaLineSegment::closest_point, and tightening is_valid would have broken CgaRect::contains, which correctly accepts huge rects.

ESCALATION: the origin-sentinel band was a symptom of a live contract violation. closest_point documents 'callers never receive a non-finite projected point' yet returned NaN for finite input -- segment (-f64::MAX,0)->(-f64::MAX,1) queried at (f64::MAX,0.5), where point.x-start.x overflows to +inf while dx is exactly 0.0, giving inf*0.0=NaN which then survives t.clamp (clamp propagates NaN).

NEGATIVE CONTROL: segment_closest_point_is_finite_for_all_finite_inputs was written and run BEFORE the fix and FAILED with 'returned non-finite CgaPoint { x: NaN, y: NaN }'. It is therefore proven to catch the defect, not a restatement of current behavior. It covers 4 shapes (dx=0 overflow, dy=0 overflow, squared-length overflow, endpoint-difference overflow) and asserts both finiteness and containment in the segment bounding box, so the origin sentinel cannot satisfy it for a well-formed segment.

FIX: existing arithmetic kept as an untouched fast path; on overflow the projection retries in a power-of-two scaled frame. Division by a power of two only shifts exponents, so no rounding is introduced and every currently-finite result stays bit-identical. distance_to_point drops its redundant overflow pre-check and delegates.

ORACLE FLIPS (2), both rejection -> real answer, both with negative controls kept:
1. rect_closest_boundary_matches_sqrt_reference pinned CgaRect::new(0,0,MAX,MAX) to origin; now asserts a real in-box boundary point. The 1e150 valid-extreme control is unchanged.
2. line_segment_closest_point_and_distance_reject_non_finite_inputs demanded INFINITY for segment (-MAX,0)->(MAX,0) at (0,0) -- a point lying exactly ON the segment, true distance 0. Also misfiled: that test's subject is non-finite input, and this segment is finite. Its genuinely non-finite cases are untouched and still fail closed.

PRECISION HONESTY: the new off-segment assertion BOUNDS rather than pins. One ULP at f64::MAX is ~2e292, so a 1.0 offset along a 3.6e308-long segment sits below the resolution of its own endpoints; the exact projection is unrepresentable and demanding it would demand precision f64 cannot carry. (My first draft asserted ==7.0 and correctly failed at 7.0710678118654755.)

NO REACHABLE BEHAVIOR CHANGE: only caller outside the module is fm-wasm hit testing (crates/fm-wasm/src/lib.rs:846), fed f32-derived layout coordinates whose squared lengths peak near 1e77 -- entirely inside the bit-identical fast path. No golden can move.

GATES (one clean sequential run on the committed source, rch remote): cargo test -p fm-core 396 pass / 0 fail (was 395, +1 new test); cargo check --workspace --all-targets RC=0 (includes fm-wasm); cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings RC=0; ubs exit 0, 0 critical, no finding on any changed line.

title: Extract layout engine into fm-layout crate
description:
Extract mermaid_layout.rs (10,656 lines) and diagram_layout.rs (3,081 lines) into fm-layout/src/. This is the core graph layout engine implementing the Sugiyama layered graph layout algorithm.

The existing 5-phase pipeline:
1. Cycle Removal: Greedy source/sink peeling with topological ordering. Tie-breaking by max (out_deg - in_deg). Returns reversed edge list for post-layout reconstruction.
2. Rank Assignment: Longest-path via Kahn's algorithm with BinaryHeap for deterministic ordering. Budget-capped iterations to handle residual cycles.
3. Crossing Minimization: Barycenter heuristic with optional sifting. Layer-by-layer refinement with position swaps. Merge-sort inversion counting O(n log n).
4. Coordinate Assignment: Median refinement with configurable spacing. Label-width-aware node sizing. Class diagram member height expansion.
5. Post-Processing: Cluster boundary computation with padding. Port resolution and attachment. Edge routing with waypoint generation. Quality scoring.

Key types: LayoutPoint, LayoutRect, LayoutNodeBox, LayoutClusterBox, LayoutEdgePath, LayoutStats, DiagramLayout, LayoutSpacing, LayoutTrace, LayoutStageSnapshot.
Key functions: layout_diagram(), layout_diagram_traced(), compute_node_sizes().

CRITICAL: Determinism guarantees must be preserved -- identical IR always produces identical layout. No RNG, no float nondeterminism, BinaryHeap<Reverse> for min-first order, deterministic tie-breaking via node ID strings.

Dependencies: fm-core only. No rendering dependencies.

comments.author: PeachGorge
comments.text:
CAPABILITY AUDIT — this epic's stated capabilities checked against its five closed children AND against the code. Result: 5 of 7 delivered, 1 partial, 1 a non-gap. One bead filed; no closed child reopened.

EPIC CLAIMS: advanced typography, shadow/gradient/glow effects, animation, icon support, responsive sizing, print optimization, overall design system coherence.
CHILDREN COVER: effects (bd-3gq.1), typography (bd-3gq.2), icons (bd-3gq.3), animation (bd-3gq.4), responsive sizing (bd-3gq.5) — all closed.
NO CHILD COVERS: print optimization, design system coherence. Those two are the audit.

1. PRINT OPTIMIZATION — PARTIAL, filed as bd-ccni. It exists and is on by default (print_optimized defaults true, print_css at lib.rs:3089 emits a real @media print block), so this is not vapourware. But measured against a live render with gradients on, the block neutralizes TEXT fill and SHAPE STROKE and gives clusters fill: #fff, while leaving node gradient fills untouched — nodes still print as fill="url(#fm-node-gradient)". Clusters get flattened for print and nodes do not, which is an internal inconsistency, not just a missing feature. Full evidence and observable acceptance criteria are on bd-ccni.

2. DESIGN SYSTEM COHERENCE — NOT A GAP, and I am recording that rather than inventing work. There IS a real CSS custom-property surface: --fm-accent-1..12, --fm-bg, --fm-edge-color, --fm-cluster-fill / -stroke / -label-color, --fm-cluster-c4-*, --fm-cluster-swimlane-*, --fm-anim-duration. Colour and animation are tokenized. What does NOT exist is spacing/radius/type-scale tokens (--fm-space, --fm-radius are absent) — but that is correct for this architecture: geometry is COMPUTED in Rust (LayoutSpacing, node sizing) and baked into coordinates, so exposing it as CSS tokens would create two sources of truth for the same numbers and let CSS silently disagree with the layout the engine already committed to. I would not file that as a gap without someone first wanting runtime restyling of geometry, which is a different feature.

SO: the epic's scope is delivered except for the print/gradient interaction. Once bd-ccni lands, every capability listed here is either implemented or consciously out of scope, and this epic can close on that basis. Not closing it myself — bd-ccni is open and its outcome is the last thing this epic is waiting on.

title: Locality-Sensitive Hashing for Approximate Nearest-Node Queries
description:
## Locality-Sensitive Hashing for Approximate Nearest-Node Queries

Implement locality-sensitive hashing (LSH) for fast approximate nearest-node queries in the rendered diagram, enabling O(1) expected-time cursor-to-node proximity detection for interactive editing and hover tooltips.

## Mathematical Foundation
LSH maps similar items (nearby 2D points) to the same hash bucket with high probability. For 2D Euclidean distance, the standard LSH family is:
  h(p) = floor((a · p + b) / w)
where a is a random unit vector, b ~ Uniform[0, w], and w is the bucket width.

**Multi-probe LSH:** Use k hash functions, concatenate their values to form a composite hash. Two points collide (land in same bucket) iff ALL k hash functions agree. Probability of collision for distance d:
  P(collision | distance=d) = (1 - d/w)^k  for d < w, 0 otherwise

**For diagram hit testing:**
Given cursor position (x, y), find the nearest node within radius r. Instead of O(n) linear scan:
1. Hash the cursor position
2. Look up the bucket → candidate nodes
3. Linear scan candidates only (typically O(1) for well-separated nodes)

**Alternative: grid-based spatial hash.** Simpler than LSH but less theoretically elegant:
- Divide viewport into w×w cells
- Each cell stores a list of nodes whose centers fall in it
- Cursor query: check the cell containing cursor + 8 neighbors
- O(1) expected time, but O(n) worst case if all nodes in one cell

**Practical consideration:** For most diagrams (< 1000 nodes), linear scan is fast enough (<1ms). LSH is only justified for 5000+ node diagrams with real-time interaction. Grid spatial hash may be the pragmatic choice.

## Key Papers
- Indyk & Motwani, "Approximate Nearest Neighbors: Towards Removing the Curse of Dimensionality" (STOC 1998)
- Andoni & Indyk, "Near-Optimal Hashing Algorithms for Approximate Nearest Neighbor" (FOCS 2006)
- Datar et al., "Locality-Sensitive Hashing Scheme Based on p-Stable Distributions" (SCG 2004) — E2LSH

## Implementation in FrankenMermaid
1. Implement simple grid spatial hash first (pragmatic baseline).
2. Implement LSH for comparison (educational value + large graph support).
3. Interface: `SpatialIndex::nearest(point, radius) -> Option<NodeId>`
4. Build spatial index after layout, invalidate on edit.
5. Use for: hover detection, click targeting, nearest-node snap in editing mode.
6. Benchmark: query time for cursor movement over 100, 1000, 10000 node diagrams.
7. Decision contract: grid hash for < 5000 nodes, LSH for >= 5000 nodes (or grid hash always if fast enough).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Grid spatial hash implementation with O(1) expected query time
- [ ] LSH implementation with configurable hash parameters
- [ ] Query correctness verified: nearest node matches brute-force result
- [ ] Query time < 0.1ms for 10000-node diagrams
- [ ] Spatial index construction time < 10ms for 10000 nodes
- [ ] Decision contract: grid hash vs LSH with measured thresholds
- [ ] WASM-compatible (no platform-specific dependencies)
close_reason: Implemented spatial indexing module (crates/fm-layout/src/spatial.rs) with: (1) GridSpatialIndex - grid-based spatial hash with configurable cell size, O(1) expected nearest/within_radius queries, handles large radii correctly, negative coordinates. (2) LshSpatialIndex - locality-sensitive hashing with p-stable distributions (normal projections), configurable bucket_width/num_hashes/num_tables, deterministic PRNG (xorshift64 + Box-Muller), multi-table probing. (3) SpatialIndex trait for polymorphic use. (4) create_spatial_index() auto-selector (grid < 5000, LSH >= 5000). 19 unit tests: grid operations, brute-force accuracy verification, negative coords, LSH nearby detection, determinism, within_radius, clear, auto-selection. All quality gates pass.

title: Fixed-iteration callgrind harness so layout instruction counts are comparable across arms
description:
Blocks every fm-layout PERF_LEDGER KEEP row that wants a counted mechanism.

THE DEFECT IN THE CURRENT METHOD. Lanes measure instructions as callgrind TOTAL Ir of a run driven by 'criterion --profile-time N'. profile-time runs for a fixed WALL duration, and under callgrind wall time is dominated by simulation cost, which is proportional to instructions executed. A cheaper arm therefore completes MORE iterations in the same window and its total lands in the same place. The metric answers 'how much work fits in N seconds', not 'what does one operation cost', so it is close to blind to the very effect it is used to certify.

MEASURED PROOF, from bd-9rq7 (whose -4.074% figure was retracted because of this):
  same command, two arms, self-reported ELFs cb674015... and fc89a91a...
    total Ir  3,038,095,487  vs  3,026,115,751   =  -0.054%
    per-iteration wall, counterbalanced           =  -2.4% and -4.3% (CIs disjoint in pass 2)
  and the SAME command on the SAME code gave ~331,360,000 total Ir on one occasion and
  ~3,038,000,000 on another — a 9x swing driven by machine conditions, not code.

WHAT TO BUILD: a bench mode that performs EXACTLY N iterations of one named workload and exits, with N fixed by argument or env and NOT derived from elapsed time. Then total Ir / N is a per-operation instruction count that is comparable across arms, deterministic, and load-independent — which is precisely what the ledger's '**Counted mechanism:**' marker is supposed to assert.

REQUIREMENTS:
1. Iteration count pinned by the caller; no wall-clock feedback anywhere in the loop.
2. Print the count it actually ran, so the divisor is in the artifact rather than assumed.
3. Keep the existing bd-x3zl ELF self-report line, so identity and count appear in the same output.
4. black_box the input and the result so the loop cannot be optimised away — a harness that measures nothing is worse than none.
5. NEGATIVE CONTROL for the harness itself: run the SAME binary twice and confirm total Ir is identical to the instruction. Callgrind is deterministic, so an A/A that is not exactly 1.000000 means the harness has nondeterminism (allocation addresses, hashing, time) and its numbers are void.

SCOPE: crates/fm-layout/benches/incremental_layout.rs to start, since that is where the retracted result lives. The same pattern serves crossing_minimization and any future layout bench.

DO NOT paper over this by re-running profile-time with a longer duration — a longer fixed wall window has exactly the same blindness. The fix is removing wall-clock from the loop-count decision.

⚠️ Any existing repo result whose evidence is 'callgrind total Ir under --profile-time' is suspect and should be re-derived once this lands.
close_reason:
Landed in b00f77d1 and immediately used to re-derive a retracted number (4c7086ef).

FM_FIXED_ITERS=N on the incremental_layout bench runs exactly N single-node label edits and exits. N is pinned by the caller, no wall clock participates in the loop count, and the workload mirrors single_node_label_edit/incremental/1000 exactly (same 2x500 IR, same warm cache, same per-iteration edit).

All five requirements from the bead met:
1. Count pinned by caller — FM_FIXED_ITERS, no wall-clock feedback.
2. Prints the count it ran (fixed_iterations=200), so the divisor is in the artifact.
3. Keeps the bd-x3zl ELF self-report, so identity and divisor appear in one output.
4. black_box on input and result, with the result consumed into a sink, so the loop cannot be optimised away.
5. Harness A/A negative control — same ELF twice must give byte-identical Ir. Verified EXACT 1.000000000 on both arms (3,084,412,314 twice; 3,065,608,265 twice).

Also exits before criterion's machinery runs, so none of it lands in the count.

PROVEN USEFUL IMMEDIATELY: the first result off it corrected bd-9rq7's fusion from a retracted -4.074% to -0.610% per edit, and made the first conforming counted-mechanism ledger row for fm-layout possible (docs/PERF_LEDGER.md:L3849, accepted by ledger_preflight --lint).

Gates: fm-layout 450 pass / 0 fail; clippy -p fm-layout --benches --features bench-internals -D warnings RC=0; ubs exit 0.

REMAINING for whoever wants it: only incremental_layout has this mode. crossing_minimization and barycenter_sweep would need the same treatment before their instruction claims are comparable, and any existing repo result evidenced as 'callgrind total Ir under --profile-time' should be re-derived through a harness like this.

title: EPIC: Intent-Reality Closure, Formal Guarantees, and Pressure-Adaptive Runtime
description:
First-principles closure epic for the gap between project intent (README/AGENTS promises) and observed runtime reality.

Background:
- README promises broad diagram support, algorithm selection, determinism, high performance, and graceful degradation.
- Current architecture is strong but has critical closure gaps: unsupported-type semantics can silently drift, layout algorithm dispatch is not fully realized, and compute-pressure degradation contracts in `fm-core` are not fully activated end-to-end.

Goal:
Deliver an "alien-artifact" quality runtime that is mathematically defensible, operationally resilient under load, and verifiably aligned with user-facing claims.

Program principles:
1. Truthfulness: every claim maps to executable evidence.
2. Determinism: same input+config => same observable outputs and diagnostics.
3. Boundedness: runtime cost remains bounded under adversarial or overloaded conditions.
4. Graceful degradation: quality degrades predictably before correctness breaks.
5. Proof-oriented optimization: only profile-backed changes with behavior proofs land.

Definition of done:
- All child issues complete with acceptance criteria satisfied.
- CI enforces correctness/performance/degradation SLO gates.
- Docs and runtime capability metadata are synchronized automatically.
- Release/canary paths are blocked on objective evidence, not manual judgment.

title: Make pie chart layout dimensions content-adaptive
description:
## What
Replace hardcoded pie chart dimensions (radius=140, label_radius=+60, cx/cy offsets) with values computed from the number of slices, label dimensions, and available space.

## Why
The pie chart layout in layout_diagram_pie_traced() (fm-layout/src/lib.rs) uses fixed dimensions:
- `radius = 140.0` — does not adapt to slice count
- `label_radius = radius + 60.0` — does not adapt to label length
- `cx = radius + 80.0`, `cy = radius + 60.0` — does not center properly with varying legend widths

With many slices (>8), labels overlap each other. With very long labels, they extend beyond the diagram bounds. With few slices, the chart is unnecessarily large.

## Proposed Approach
1. Compute `radius` from: `max(100.0, min(200.0, slice_count * 20.0))`
2. Compute `label_radius` from: `radius + max_label_width * 0.5 + 20.0`
3. Compute `cx`/`cy` to center the pie within the computed bounds
4. Consider adding `PieLayoutConfig` struct to LayoutConfig with `min_radius`, `max_radius`, `label_padding` fields

## Acceptance Criteria
- Pie charts with 2-3 slices are compact
- Pie charts with 15+ slices are larger with readable labels
- Labels never overlap (or at least minimize overlap with angle-based spreading)
- No regression for typical (3-8 slice) pie charts
close_reason: Pie radius now scales with slice count: base_radius=100+8*n, clamped to [80,220]. Label radius and center computed from radius. Replaces fixed 140/60/80/60.

title: Class member shorthand 'Class : +member' renders as a literal node label
description:
Found incidentally while checking bd-4isi golden fallout (cc lane, LilacPike).

crates/fm-cli/tests/golden/class_basic.mmd is:
  classDiagram
    Animal <|-- Dog
    Animal : +name
    Dog : +bark()

The committed golden SVG (crates/fm-cli/tests/golden/class_basic.svg) contains exactly two text
elements: 'Animal : +name' and 'Dog'. So the colon shorthand does NOT populate class_meta.attributes
-- it becomes a literal node LABEL containing the whole line -- and 'Dog : +bark()' contributes no
visible text at all ('bark' appears zero times in the golden).

mermaid-js renders this as a class box 'Animal' with a member row '+name', and a box 'Dog' with
'+bark()'. So this is a real cross-engine fidelity gap, in the same family as bd-4isi but on a
DIFFERENT code path: bd-4isi was block syntax ('class C { +int f }') whose members reached
class_meta but were truncated by node sizing; this is shorthand whose members never reach class_meta
at all.

NOT currently blocking any measured claim. The head-to-head corpora (corpus.mjs classDiagram() and
docClass()) both emit BLOCK syntax, so ci_batch_500 / doc_build_40 / docs_site_* do not exercise this
path. Verified bd-4isi's fix does not change class_basic output: baseline ELF 3d081db7 and fixed ELF
3ed92bc5 both render it to SHA-256 fcf194be77fdd22e71e9e0ed2bd737c691ab91f8a2a082140ffeda5a80b5343b,
so golden_svg_test is unaffected by that fix.

Retry predicate: raise priority if any timed corpus starts emitting colon-shorthand members, or if
the equivalence gate is extended to a corpus that uses it.

comments.text:

parse_class_shorthand_member splits 'Animal : +name' on the FIRST colon and emits BlockStart/Member/End, reusing the existing block lowering so members reach class_meta. Guard: left of the colon must be a single whitespace-free token (excludes 'style A fill:#f00', 'classDef x fill:#f00', 'link A "http://x"', 'note for A "text: here"'), plus accTitle/accDescr/title/direction by name. Runs AFTER the edge attempt so 'A <|-- B : label' still parses as an edge.

  before: 'Animal : +name', 'Dog'   <- whole line as one literal label; 'bark' absent entirely
  after:  'Animal', '+name', 'Dog', '+bark()'

title: class diagram members are dropped from rendered SVG
description:
Measured against mermaid-js 11.15.0 on identical input (class_50, 50 classes each with one field and one method):

  render                     class names  +int fieldN  methodN
  mermaid-js 11.15.0              50          50         50
  frankenmermaid CLI              50          50          0
  frankenmermaid bench harness    50           0          0

Two independent defects:
1. Class METHODS are never rendered on any path or at any size.
2. Class FIELDS render at 2 classes but vanish at 50 in the headtohead bench path. The CLI renders them at 50 only because its guardrail forced tree -> sugiyama, so member rendering is layout-algorithm dependent (same failure shape as bd-1buv mindmap Radial/Tree dispatch).

Impact on published numbers: class is 1/5 of ci_batch_500 and doc_build_40, so the certified CI-batch ratios compare mermaid's full render against our partial one for 100 of 500 diagrams. Detected by the bd-evx6 equivalence gate: node.members is populated in the IR (fm-render-svg/src/lib.rs ~5600, ~5882 iterate it), so this is a render/layout-sizing gate, not a parse gap.

Not a render bug. crates/fm-layout/src/lib.rs compute_node_size() measured ONLY the node label -- it

advances a cursor per member row and does 'if cursor_y > y + h - line_h*0.5 { break }', so rows that

arithmetic (stereotype, name, separators, row height = line_height_px*0.81, guard slack) plus half a

member row. node_size_cache_key now hashes members, else an incremental edit to a class body would

title: Implement sequence diagram autonumber
description:

\`\`\`
sequenceDiagram

  Alice->>Bob: First (1)

title: EPIC: Reality Check Gap Closure
description:
## Purpose
Close every gap identified in the 2026-04-09 reality check audit. The audit compared README/AGENTS.md promises against actual code, tests, and deployment state. While the project is substantially honest (86k lines, all 24 diagram types render, all CLI commands work), several gaps threaten credibility:

1. **npm install claim is false**: @frankenmermaid/core returns 404 on npm registry. README tells users to run `npm install @frankenmermaid/core` which will fail.
2. **install.sh never committed**: README's `curl -fsSL .../install.sh | bash` links to a file that doesn't exist on GitHub (untracked locally).
3. **classDef/style directives silently dropped**: Parsed but never applied to SVG render output. Users can write `classDef` and see no effect — no error, no warning, just silent failure.
4. **README understates FNX integration status**: Described as optional feature flag; actually the project's largest unfinished initiative (~25 open P1 beads).
5. **Long-tail diagram fidelity unproven**: All 16 tested types produce valid SVG, but visual quality (correct layout for sankey flows, pie slice angles, gitGraph branch lanes) has no golden-test coverage.
6. **Sequence advanced features incomplete**: Activation boxes, interaction fragments (alt/opt/loop), and notes are only partially parsed.
7. **Working tree hygiene**: Dozens of untracked audit files cluttering git status (fixed by .gitignore update in this session).

## Relationship to Existing Work
- FNX integration has its own epic (bd-ml2r); this epic does NOT duplicate that. Instead we create a single bead for README honesty about FNX status.
- Typography work (bd-3gq.2) is in progress; classDef styling is a SEPARATE concern (parsed→rendered wiring, not font metrics).
- "Write README" bead exists but covers feature comparison, not factual accuracy of install instructions.

## Success Criteria
- Every README install instruction either works or is corrected.
- classDef/style directives produce visible output in SVG or emit a diagnostic explaining they're unsupported.
- Golden tests added for at least 6 long-tail diagram types.
- Sequence advanced features either work or are honestly documented as unsupported.
- README FNX section accurately describes current state.

3. classDef/style silently dropped — FIXED. collect_classdef_css emits .fm-node-user-<slug> rules and the renderer references them in 16 places.

5. Long-tail fidelity — THE ONE STILL STANDING, but its stated reason is wrong and the correction matters. Coverage is NOT missing: 37 fixtures span 21 diagram types INCLUDING sankey-beta, pie and gitGraph, the exact three the audit named. What is missing is SEMANTIC FORCE. Of 21 types, two have a guard proving output is CORRECT rather than merely UNCHANGED — gantt_basic (bd-uay6) and now pie_basic (26c76635). The other 19 are pinned by FNV byte hash alone, and a byte hash blesses a wrong picture as readily as a right one. Filed as bd-iicc with prioritised targets and the standard a guard must meet.

title: Replace hardcoded diagram title color in scene renderer
description:
## What
Replace hardcoded dark gray (#1f2937) for diagram titles in the scene-based render path (render_scene_document_with_ir) with a theme-aware value.

## Why
The scene-based renderer at fm-render-svg/src/lib.rs line ~341 uses `.fill("#1f2937")` for diagram titles. This dark color is invisible on Dark, Blueprint, and Neon themes.

## Technical Context
This is in `render_scene_document_with_ir()` where the title is rendered BEFORE `let theme = resolve_theme()` at line ~361. The theme is not yet available when the title is rendered.

## Options
1. **Move title rendering after theme resolution** — requires restructuring the function, since the title needs to be in the SVG before the main content for z-ordering
2. **Use CSS custom property** — `.fill("var(--fm-text-color, #1f2937)")` — works when theme CSS is embedded
3. **Pre-resolve theme for title** — call `resolve_theme()` earlier just for the title color

Option 2 is the simplest and most robust since the theme CSS block IS embedded before the title element.

## Specific Changes
- fm-render-svg/src/lib.rs line ~341: Change `.fill("#1f2937")` to `.fill("var(--fm-text-color, #1f2937)")`

## Acceptance Criteria
- Diagram titles are readable on all 10 theme presets
- No visual regression on Default theme (fallback is the same dark gray)
close_reason: Title now uses var(--fm-text-color, #1f2937) CSS custom property. Theme CSS defines --fm-text-color for all presets.

title: gitGraph branches render collinear; commits on different branches share one lane
description:
Found by bd-iicc while writing a semantic guard for the gitGraph golden. Same class as bd-e69x: the byte golden pins it happily because the output is stable, it is just not a gitGraph.

MEASURED on crates/fm-cli/tests/golden/gitgraph_basic.svg at HEAD:

  fixture: 2 commits on main, branch develop, 2 commits on develop, merge back, 1 more on main
  rendered: 6 commit circles at 6 distinct cy values (a vertical chain)
  rendered cx values across ALL commits: 158.52 and 176.26 only
  branch tags in order: git-branch-0, git-branch-0, git-branch-1, git-branch-1, git-branch-0
  no transform attributes anywhere in the file, so these are final coordinates

Commits tagged git-branch-1 (develop) sit at the SAME x as commits tagged git-branch-0 (main). The two branches are drawn collinear.

WHY THIS IS A DEFECT, not a layout preference. Distinct lanes are the visual grammar of a gitGraph: the reader identifies which commits belong to which branch by their lane, and a merge is legible precisely because it joins two lanes. Collapsed onto one column, the diagram cannot express what it exists to express — the branch structure is present in the CLASS attribute but invisible in the picture. mermaid-js assigns each branch its own lane, so this is also a cross-engine fidelity gap.

WHAT IS ALREADY RIGHT, so nobody re-does it: parsing and branch attribution are sound. All six commits render, they are ordered correctly down the chain, and branch membership is correctly recorded in the fm-node-user-git-branch-N class — the information reaches the renderer intact. The gap is purely that lane index is not converted into a position.

ODDITY WORTH CHECKING while fixing, not filed separately because I did not confirm it is wrong: only FIVE of the six circles carry a git-branch-N class. The untagged one is at cy=679.25, positionally where the merge commit falls, and it is also the only commit at the outlier cx=176.26. A merge commit legitimately belongs to the target branch, so it may simply be tagged differently on purpose — but if it is an accidental omission, the same fix should cover it.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA, observable:
1. Commits sharing a branch tag share a lane coordinate: all git-branch-0 commits at one x, all git-branch-1 commits at another.
2. Different branches occupy DIFFERENT lanes - the branch-0 lane and branch-1 lane differ by at least a commit diameter, so the lanes are visually separable rather than merely unequal by a rounding error.
3. Ordering along the chain is preserved: the fix must not reorder commits to achieve separation.
4. GOLDEN IMPACT: gitgraph_basic.svg will move, and its viewBox will likely widen to accommodate a second lane. That is a legitimate GOLDEN-CHANGE needing a semantic diff that names the new lane positions and confirms no commit was lost or reordered. Only the gitGraph fixture should move.

TEST ALREADY WRITTEN AND WAITING: bd-iicc adds gitgraph_branches_occupy_distinct_lanes, currently #[ignore]d with a pointer to this bead. UN-IGNORING IT IS THIS BEAD'S ACCEPTANCE GATE. Do not weaken it to make it pass - in particular do not relax the lane-separation distance to whatever the fix happens to produce.
close_reason:
Fixed by 42286916. ROOT CAUSE: layout_diagram_gitgraph_traced assigned lanes from CLUSTER membership, which a gitGraph never populates, so every commit fell into lane 0. The git-branch-N class could not serve as the lane because that index is taken modulo the 8-colour palette (branch 8 would land on branch 0's lane); new fm_core::IrGitGraphMeta carries the unwrapped lane per commit node, published by the parser and consumed by layout. memo_ir_equal's destructuring guard forced the new field into the incremental equality probe at compile time.

THREE SUB-DEFECTS fixed alongside, each of which also produced a lane-0 collision: (1) the ODDITY THE BEAD FLAGGED was an accidental omission - merge AND cherry-pick commits carried no branch attribution at all; all three commit paths now route through one tag_git_commit_branch helper, so the merge commit is tagged git-branch-0 (the branch it merged into) and branch tags go 5 -> 6. (2) checkout of an undeclared branch fell through branch_index's unwrap_or(0) and aliased onto main; it now interns its own lane. (3) commits were left-aligned in their lane, so a wide 'merge develop' box sat at a different centre from a bare commit on the same branch - that is why the merge was the outlier at cx=176.26. Commits are now centred across the lane.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA, all met and measured on the rendered fixture:
1. Same branch, same lane: the four git-branch-0 commits are all at cx=176.26; the two git-branch-1 commits are both at cx=424.79.
2. Different lanes, visually separable: 248.53 apart vs a 66.5 commit diameter.
3. Ordering preserved: 6 circles at the SAME six cy values as before (125.25 / 263.75 / 402.25 / 540.75 / 679.25 / 817.75); none lost, added, or reordered. Edge paths now traverse 176.26 <-> 424.79 at both the fork and the merge.
4. GOLDEN-CHANGE with semantic diff: gitgraph_basic.svg viewBox 352.53 -> 583.31 wide (height unchanged at 943), layout_checksums.json gitgraph_basic layout_width 272.53 -> 503.31. BLESS ran over all 19 SVG cases and 22 layout cases and ONLY the gitGraph fixture moved - every other checksum byte-identical.

ACCEPTANCE GATE: golden_svg_test::gitgraph_branches_occupy_distinct_lanes un-ignored with its assertions UNCHANGED - the separation threshold was not relaxed.

TESTS (same bead, 4 new + 1 un-ignored): fm-layout gitgraph_commits_are_placed_in_their_branch_lane asserts the geometric property (same branch -> same centre, different branch -> >= one diameter, chain order monotonic) rather than pinning coordinates; 3 fm-parser tests - lane for every commit incl. merge/cherry-pick cross-checked against the palette class, checkout-only branch gets its own lane, lanes stay distinct past 9 branches while the class provably wraps to git-branch-1.

NEGATIVE CONTROLS proving the tests catch the defect rather than restating the code: lane forced to 0 -> layout test fails 'lanes 124.262505 and 124.262505 are closer than one commit diameter (66.5)'; merge tagging removed -> 'every commit needs a lane, got {0: 0, 1: 1, 3: 0} for 4 nodes'; checkout interning removed -> branches ["main"] vs ["main", "feature"]. Both touched source files restored byte-identically (diff -q) after each control.

GATES: cargo check --workspace --all-targets clean (rch remote vmi1152480); cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings clean (rch remote ovh-a); cargo test --workspace 40/40 suites green, 0 failures; fm-parser gitgraph 21/21, fm-layout target 1/1, golden_svg_test 8/8, golden_layout_test 2/2; ubs exit 0 with no finding in the new code; cargo fmt --check shows zero drift in any hunk this commit authored; pre-commit hook chain (40-ledger-integrity, 50-agent-mail) both exit 0. Pushed to main and master at 42286916.

title: Wire classDef/style directives through to SVG render output
description:
## Problem
Mermaid classDef and style directives are PARSED by fm-parser (confirmed: the parser extracts class definitions and style assignments into the IR) but they are NEVER APPLIED during SVG rendering. This means:
- A user writes: `classDef important fill:#f9f,stroke:#333,stroke-width:4px`
- The parser stores this in the IR without error
- The SVG renderer completely ignores it
- The user sees default styling with NO warning or diagnostic

This is a silent failure — worse than a "not supported" error because the user doesn't know their styling is being dropped.

## Scope
1. **Survey the IR**: Determine where classDef data lives in MermaidDiagramIr after parsing. Check IrNode.classes, any classDef-specific structures in meta, and style directive handling.
2. **SVG render integration**: In fm-render-svg, when rendering a node, check if it has classes that match any classDef. If so, apply the CSS properties (fill, stroke, stroke-width, color, font-size, etc.) to the SVG element's inline style or as CSS custom properties.
3. **CSS generation**: Generate <style> rules in the SVG <defs> section for each classDef, scoped to the appropriate CSS selectors (e.g., `.node.important { fill: #f9f; }`).
4. **Style directive handling**: Wire the `style` directive (which applies inline styles to specific nodes) through to SVG output.
5. **Theme interaction**: Define precedence: theme defaults < classDef rules < inline style directives < init directive overrides. Document this.
6. **Diagnostic for partial support**: If any CSS property in a classDef is not supported by the SVG renderer, emit a Warning-level diagnostic listing the unsupported properties.

## Why This Matters
Styling is one of the most-used Mermaid features. Users migrating from mermaid-js will expect classDef to work. Silent failure erodes trust more than explicit "unsupported" errors.

## Dependencies
- fm-parser already parses classDef (verified).
- fm-core IR must carry the parsed data (verify exact fields).
- fm-render-svg must consume and apply it.

## Testing
- Unit test: classDef with fill/stroke/stroke-width produces matching SVG attributes.
- Unit test: style directive on specific node overrides classDef.
- Golden test: `flowchart_with_classdef.mmd` added to golden suite.
- Negative test: unsupported CSS property emits diagnostic.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `classDef` definitions in Mermaid input produce visible style changes in SVG output.
- `style` directives on individual nodes produce visible inline styles.
- Unsupported CSS properties emit a warning diagnostic.
- Golden test captures the styled output for regression safety.
- README Limitations section updated to remove classDef from the "not yet applied" list.
close_reason: classDef/style already fully implemented; added golden test flowchart_classdef.mmd/.svg

title: Local cargo builds silently link stale rch-retrieved artifacts
description:
Found the hard way by cc lane (LilacPike) after drawing a wrong conclusion from a stale binary.

SYMPTOM: a local 'cargo build -p frankenmermaid-cli --example headtohead' prints only
'Compiling frankenmermaid-cli' and 'Finished' in ~25s, produces a working binary, and that binary
contains a THREE-WEEK-OLD parser. Source changes to fm-parser are silently ignored.

EVIDENCE:
  crates/fm-parser/src/mermaid_parser.rs  mtime 2026-07-31
  target/release/deps/libfm_parser-*.rlib mtime 2026-07-10 .. 2026-07-13
  cargo clean -p fm-parser  ->  'Removed 0 files'
  touch mermaid_parser.rs + rebuild -> IDENTICAL ELF sha256 (317f66e9...)

CAUSE: rch exec retrieves the worker's build artifacts into the local target/ (it reported
'384 files, 1828357 bytes' on one run). Those arrive with fingerprints cargo treats as fresh, so a
subsequent LOCAL cargo build considers fm-parser up to date and links the remote-built rlib. cargo
clean -p cannot remove them because they are not tracked as locally-built units.

WHY IT MATTERS: this manufactures false measurement and false verdicts. I ran the cross-engine
equivalence gate on ci_docs_2000 with such a binary and got 105 divergent state diagrams -- exactly
the PRE-FIX count -- and briefly took it as evidence that a committed, unit-tested fix did not work.
Same failure class as the 'verify fm_elf_sha256 MOVED' rule already in the rch overlay guidance; that
rule exists for overlay mistakes, but this is a plain local build.

MITIGATION THAT WORKS: build through rch (--base <sha> --clean-overlay), which uses a clean remote
tree, and ALWAYS verify the ELF sha256 moved before trusting any run.

WANTED: either make local builds refuse to link rch-retrieved units, or have rch retrieve into a
directory that local cargo does not consult, or document a supported 'make local target consistent'
step. Note test-profile builds appeared UNAFFECTED in the same tree -- they rebuilt correctly and
produced fixed output -- so the staleness is per-profile/unit and easy to miss.
notes:
SHARPER DIAGNOSIS (cc lane, LilacPike): CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/data/tmp/cargo-target is set in the agent environment.

So there are TWO target trees in play:
  /data/projects/frankenmermaid/target/   <- where rch RETRIEVES worker-built artifacts
  /data/tmp/cargo-target/                 <- where local cargo actually builds (CARGO_TARGET_DIR)

That explains the whole confusing picture:
- 'cargo clean -p fm-parser' reported 'Removed 0 files' because it cleaned the CARGO_TARGET_DIR tree,
  which is not where the stale rch artifacts live.
- The stale libfm_parser-*.rlib files I found dated Jul 10-13 are in the repo's target/deps, i.e. the
  rch retrieval target, and were never what local cargo was linking.
- The rch recipes all use 'env -u CARGO_TARGET_DIR', which UNSETS it so rch can rewrite it to a
  worker-scoped path. A plain local cargo invocation does NOT unset it and uses the shared tree.

I have not re-established exactly which tree produced the stale headtohead binary, so the original
title may be imprecise. What IS reproducible and matters: a local 'cargo build --example headtohead'
produced a binary whose parser behaved PRE-FIX while the test profile in the same checkout behaved
POST-FIX, and touching the source did not change the resulting ELF sha256. Whatever the mechanism,
the operational rule stands: build through rch and VERIFY THE ELF SHA MOVED before trusting a run.

Also correcting myself: commit messages 4e93cd76 and 98043420 say the local bless reused 'the repo's
existing target/'. It did not -- it used the shared /data/tmp/cargo-target. Still one pre-existing
shared directory with nothing newly minted, so the disk directive was satisfied, but the wording is
wrong.

title: bd-2gr9: evidenced Swiss-Tables target = LayoutDependencyGraph BTreeMap probes (1.91% incremental), gated on an iteration-order audit
description:
bd-2gr9 asks for Swiss/Fx hash maps in the graph IR but names no measured target. This one is measured.

EVIDENCE (deterministic callgrind, single_node_label_edit/incremental/1000, ELF 6cd47a15a0cb01f7bdb422e91792f292fa838b7b1b4746035d8da6a9d1b663b7):
  LayoutDependencyGraph::from_ir  1.91% self, attributed to
  library/alloc/src/collections/btree/search.rs
i.e. the cost is B-tree DESCENTS, not the work from_ir does. Also visible in the same profile:
  BTreeMap<SubgraphRegionId,_>::IntoIter::dying_next  0.77%

SURFACE (crates/fm-layout/src/lib.rs:222):
  regions: BTreeMap<SubgraphRegionId, SubgraphRegion>
  index:   BTreeMap<RegionInput, BTreeSet<SubgraphRegionId>>
plus BTreeMap/BTreeSet locals inside from_ir (explicit_region_ids, covered_nodes).

⚠️ HARD PRECONDITION — DO NOT SKIP. This repo mandates deterministic layout, and BTreeMap iterates in key order while FxHashMap does not. The one landed precedent (72ffc1f, node_size_cache BTreeMap -> FxHashMap) was safe for a specific stated reason: that map is lookup-only and carries an in-code comment saying so ('never iterated for output', lib.rs ~1086). These maps are NOT obviously in that class — dirty-region propagation reads them, and if region iteration order reaches node ordering or edge routing, a hash map silently makes layout nondeterministic. That is a correctness regression that goldens may not even catch reliably, since a hash map can happen to iterate stably within one run.

REQUIRED ORDER OF WORK:
1. AUDIT every read of regions/index and prove whether iteration order can reach output. Write the answer down. If any path can, either keep the BTreeMap or sort at the boundary and re-measure with the sort included (a sort may eat the entire 1.91%).
2. Only then swap, and only the maps the audit cleared.
3. Determinism probe as a NEGATIVE CONTROL: layout the same input N times in one process and assert byte-identical output. Run it against the PRE-change binary too — if it passes there and after, it proves nothing unless it can fail; construct it so a deliberately nondeterministic iteration order makes it red.
4. Instruction-gate the result. The substrate is in place: callgrind (perf is dead here, perf_event_paranoid=4), A/A null came out EXACTLY 1.000000 on this bench, and incremental_layout now self-reports its ELF as of 5b0ff735 so a KEEP row is finally writable.

CEILING: 1.91% + 0.77%. Do not expect more, and do not widen the swap beyond what the audit clears to chase a bigger number. Related: [[project_layout_stable_priorities_hoist_and_mimalloc_profile]] PROBE TAXONOMY — the cheapest outcome is often DELETING a probe rather than making it faster, so check first whether these lookups are needed at all.
close_reason:
AUDIT DONE (step 1 of this bead's required order) — and it REFUTES the swap. No code changed; the deliverable is the finding.

VERDICT PER MAP:

1. LayoutDependencyGraph.regions (BTreeMap<SubgraphRegionId, SubgraphRegion>) — ORDERING IS LOAD-BEARING. NOT swappable.
   Of all .regions() callers, only two ITERATE (lib.rs:3368 and :3484) and both are order-INSENSITIVE — they insert into a BTreeSet and sum a count, so the result is identical under any order. That part looked safe. The blocker is elsewhere: the test at lib.rs:15716, layout_dependency_graph_prefers_explicit_subgraphs_then_connectivity_fragments, iterates .regions().values() and asserts an EXACT ORDERED sequence. Its name states that the order IS the property. SubgraphRegionId is assigned in construction order (explicit subgraphs first, then connectivity fragments), so the BTreeMap's key ordering is the mechanism that encodes it. FxHashMap would destroy it, and rewriting that assertion to accept the new order would be gate self-weakening on a named behavioural property. Nearby lib.rs:15755 layout_dependency_graph_build_is_deterministic_for_identical_ir guards the same area.
   A hash map here would require a parallel Vec<SubgraphRegionId> to carry enumeration order — real complexity for the ceiling below.

2. LayoutDependencyGraph.index (BTreeMap<RegionInput, BTreeSet<SubgraphRegionId>>) — SWAPPABLE. Sole use is .get(&edit.input()).cloned() at lib.rs:409; its BTreeSet value is extended into a DirtySet, which is order-insensitive. Never iterated.

3. explicit_region_ids (local in from_ir) — SWAPPABLE. Only .insert() and .get(&parent.0).copied(). Never iterated. Same class as the 72ffc1f node_size_cache precedent.

4. covered_nodes / recursive_members / node_indexes (BTreeSets) — NOT swappable. node_indexes is iterated into ordered Vecs that feed layout_bounds_for_members and thus geometry.

5. DirtySet.regions is a BTreeSet and MUST stay one: it is iterated at lib.rs:415, 1540, 3388, 3506 and 3624, and those iterations reach node geometry and the reported dirty-region rectangles. It was never the target but is easy to hit by accident while editing this area.

CEILING AFTER THE AUDIT: the swappable set is items 2 and 3 only. The measured 1.91% is LayoutDependencyGraph::from_ir self time attributed to btree/search.rs, and the bulk of that is the BTreeSet work in items 4 plus the regions map in item 1 — none of which may move. Items 2 and 3 are a handful of probes per subgraph. Expected well under 1%, i.e. a predicted wash, which is why no swap was implemented rather than implementing one and measuring a wash.

Both key types already derive Hash, so the mechanical blocker is absent — the blocker is semantic.

RETRY PREDICATE: implement items 2 and 3 only if a profile attributes >=1% specifically to those two probe sites (not to from_ir as a whole), and gate it on instructions with the callgrind substrate (A/A null was EXACTLY 1.000000 on this bench; incremental_layout self-reports its ELF as of 5b0ff735, so a KEEP row is now writable). Do NOT touch item 1 without first replacing the ordering contract with an explicit ordered structure AND keeping the lib.rs:15716 assertion exactly as written.

title: LEVER (surface): spatial index for edge-routing obstacles — O(E*V) -> O(E*k), ~60% of large-flowchart layout
description: Profiled large-flowchart layout (frankenmermaid-cc): large_500 uses Tree algo (guardrail fallback). TREE_TIMING breakdown (us): sizes=107, tree_struct=79, spans+centers=28, boxes=91, EDGE_PATHS=476 (~60%), post=19. Edge routing dominates. Root cause: route_edge_points_with_obstacles (lib.rs:11208) calls cga_routing::find_horizontal/vertical_segment_nudge (cga_routing.rs:155/90) ~1-2x per edge, each scanning ALL ~V node-obstacles (my AABB prefilter rejects cheaply but still VISITS all V). So O(E*V) ~ 375k visits for 500 edges. LEVER: spatial index (grid / Y-band bucket) so each segment queries only nearby obstacles -> O(E*k). CONSTRAINTS for output-identity: (1) find_*_segment_nudge returns the FIRST intersecting obstacle in slice order (cga_routing.rs:205) -> the index must return candidates and pick MIN original index; (2) build_edge_paths_with_orientation parks source/target via FAR_AWAY sentinel per edge (obstacle_bounds mutated) -> the index stores indices and the nudge must read current (parked) obstacle_bounds[i], so parked endpoints AABB-reject correctly. Conservative-superset query = output-identical (verify 426 fm-layout tests + snapshots). REJECTED this turn: per-edge bbox pre-filter (nudge called only ~1-2x/edge, so filtering O(V) once doesn't beat 1-2 scans); singleton-rank skip (~0, wrong path). compute_node_sizes Cow (avoid 500 label clones) is micro (~3% of tree). Note: edge routing is contended (cod-a/TanSparrow), coordinate with reservations.

title: Tighten layout_svg_capacity_hint (over-reserves 1.33-2.08x); the large-diagram 'double-copy' is only ~3.4% of render
description:
PARKED, ANALYSIS-ONLY. Full write-up: tests/artifacts/perf/PARKED_large_render_capacity_and_double_copy.md

FINDING (corrects the 2026-07-04 DIG frontier map). No pinned corpus item reaches the large slow path: the streaming gate is 'edges < 4096 && nodes < 2048' (lib.rs:2892) and the corpus tops out at 512 nodes. Generated wide_40x80 (3200 nodes / 6201 edges / 3,475,207 B output) and profiled it.

memmove+memcpy is 2.54% of the whole pipeline (<=11.7% of render, consistent with cod_fm's 14.82% on the render-only bench). But the folded call-chains show it is NOT mostly the double copy:
  0.72%  unresolved kernel chain -- page-fault/zeroing of the multi-MB output buffer
  0.72%  __memcpy_avx (inlined, unattributed)
  0.37%  write_common_node_fragment_into::<true> -> String::write_fmt   (streaming buffer GROWTH, not a copy)
  0.37%  alloc::str::join_generic_copy                                   (copy 1: chunks -> node_svg/edge_svg)
  0.36%  Element::write_to_string -> push_str                            (copy 2: raw_svg_parts -> final String)

=> the identifiable double-copy is ~0.73% of pipeline ~= 3.4% of render.

NO-SHIP the rope/arena output contract (the escape hatch named in render_large_raw_part_body_fusion_NEGATIVE.md). It is a PUBLIC API change to render_svg_with_layout's return type and buys at most ~3.4% of render. This also explains all three prior rejections at once (large to_string_with_body 2026-07-05; raw-part body fusion +22.65% regression; empty between-child guards flat) -- each attacked a ~0.4% frame.

WHAT THE PROFILE DOES SUPPORT: finish_layout_svg_document presizes via layout_svg_capacity_hint = 16 KiB + 768*nodes + 384*edges + 512*clusters + 192*aux (lib.rs:3187/3202). It never under-reserves; it OVER-reserves 1.33-2.08x on every measured item:
  small_10 2.08x | medium_100 1.81x | large_500 1.72x | wide_8x16 1.49x | wide_16x32 1.46x | dense_dag_200 1.33x | wide_40x80 1.40x (4,855,168 B hint vs 3,475,207 B actual = 1.38 MB of surplus pages the kernel maps+zeroes -- exactly the 0.72% kernel chain).

LEVER: tighten NODE_BYTES(768)/EDGE_BYTES(384). Byte-identical BY CONSTRUCTION (only affects String::with_capacity). DO NOT move the constants on this table alone: a hint that is too SMALL costs a realloc + full-buffer memmove, strictly worse than over-reserving, and the corpus generators emit short labels. Measure against a label-heavy corpus first. Also unknown: whether mimalloc actually faults in the surplus.

BLOCKER (why parked): no valid A/B substrate today.
 * local cargo bench prohibited (disk at 96%);
 * rch exec CANNOT carry a split A/B -- it exposes no worker-pinning flag and picks workers non-deterministically (confirmed: RCH_WORKER=hz1 was silently ignored, both arms ran on hz2). See the CORRECTION entry in docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md.
 * the prescribed one-binary/one-invocation alternating criterion substrate is not expressible: layout_svg_capacity_hint is private and capacity is not a parameter of any public entry point.

UNPARK BY: (1) thread the hint through a bench-only parameter on render_svg_with_layout and register hint_current vs hint_tight as two arms of ONE criterion group in crates/fm-cli/benches/pipeline_bench.rs, run in a single rch exec invocation; or (2) wait for the disk constraint to lift and use the machine-local 'perf stat -e instructions:u' two-point A/B with a code-layout control (the substrate that carried bd-w5sn; it resolved a 0.03% effect and is immune to both the worker-selection problem and the +/-5% code-layout roulette). Option 2 preferred.

FILE-OWNERSHIP: crates/fm-render-svg/src/lib.rs (capacity hint region ~3187-3230).
close_reason:
REJECTED on measurement (cc_fm, 2026-07-10). The premise was wrong and it was MY premise: I claimed the 1.38 MB of over-reserved capacity was 'surplus pages the kernel maps and zeroes -- precisely the 0.72% kernel chain'. That was inference, never measured.

MEASURED (wide_40x80, 3200 nodes / 6201 edges / 3,475,207 B output, perf stat two-point delta reps 36-6, 60 renders per delta, FM_H2H_FORCE_PROFILE=default):
  page-faults  delta 886  -> 14.8 per render
  minor-faults delta 917  -> 15.3 per render
Against: bytes written 3,475,207 = 848 pages; hint reservation 4,855,168 = 1,185 pages; surplus = 336 pages.
14.8 faults/render -- NOT 848, NOT 1,185.

MECHANISM: String::with_capacity(n) calls malloc(n) and does NOT touch the memory; pages fault lazily on first WRITE, so the 336-page surplus is never touched. And mimalloc RECYCLES the 3.47 MB buffer between renders rather than munmap/refault, so even the written pages fault once and the two-point delta cancels them. The over-reservation is FREE.

Tightening NODE_BYTES/EDGE_BYTES therefore saves nothing on the upside and risks a realloc + whole-buffer memmove on the downside. An under-reserving hint is strictly worse than an over-reserving one. DO NOT RETRY unless a profile shows non-zero per-render fault cost attributable to the output buffer.

SELF-TIME RECORDED. memmove+memcpy = 2.54% of sampled pipeline, dominant chain String::write_fmt / push_str -> copy_nonoverlapping = BUFFER APPEND (the unavoidable act of writing bytes), not a redundant copy. The identifiable double copy is join_generic_copy 0.37% + Element::write_to_string 0.36% = 0.73% of pipeline ~= 3.4% of render. Kernel frames total 18.27% and are NOT output-buffer faults; dwarf call-graph sampling overhead is the plausible bulk.

ALSO SETTLED: the three double-copy rejections PASS the ledger-integrity rule (unlike the 4/4 crossing-min failures). large_wide_stages/render/40x80 builds gen_wide(40,80) = 3200 nodes, and the streaming gate is nodes < 2048, so the large slow path DOES execute. The rejections are evidence about live code and they hold.

AND: the double-copy frame provably did not move. wide_40x80 default-profile pipeline instructions: 830d672 1.0000x -> bc56f72 0.9984x -> 0f9efd4 0.9984x. Both landings are structural no-ops on the large path. Lean profile: 0.7274x (-27.3%), the biggest measured effect of the edge-fragment lever anywhere.

Evidence: .benchmarks/render_capacity_preshaping_NEGATIVE.md

title: Quotient Filters for Fast Duplicate Edge Detection
description:
## Quotient Filters for Fast Duplicate Edge Detection

Use quotient filters (a cache-friendly alternative to Bloom filters) to detect duplicate edges during graph construction, enabling O(1) amortized duplicate detection with minimal memory overhead.

## Mathematical Foundation
A quotient filter stores a set of fingerprints compactly using quotienting: for hash h(x), split into quotient q and remainder r where h(x) = q * 2^r_bits + r. Store remainder r in slot q of a compact array, using linear probing for collisions. Properties:
- Space: ~10-25% less than Bloom filters at the same false positive rate
- Cache behavior: elements stored in contiguous sorted runs → excellent locality
- False positive rate: 2^{-r_bits} (configurable via remainder size)
- No false negatives: if element was inserted, it will be found

**For duplicate edge detection:**
When parsing a Mermaid diagram, each edge (u, v) must be checked for duplicates. For n edges:
- Naive HashSet: O(n) space, O(1) per lookup, but HashSet overhead per entry
- Quotient filter: O(n * r_bits / 8) bytes, O(1) per lookup, much lower constant factor
- For r_bits = 16: false positive rate = 1/65536, space = 2 bytes per edge
- For 10000 edges: quotient filter = ~20KB vs HashSet = ~400KB (20x savings)

**Practical consideration:** The space savings are significant for WASM target where memory is constrained. For native target, the HashSet overhead is negligible. This is primarily a WASM optimization.

## Key Papers
- Bender et al., "Don't Thrash: How to Cache Your Hash on Flash" (VLDB 2012) — quotient filter
- Pandey et al., "A General-Purpose Counting Filter" (SIGMOD 2017) — counting quotient filter
- Fan et al., "Cuckoo Filter: Practically Better Than Bloom" (CoNEXT 2014) — alternative approach

## Implementation in FrankenMermaid
1. Implement `QuotientFilter<H>` generic over hash function.
2. Use FxHash for fingerprint computation (fast, non-cryptographic).
3. Implement `insert(edge_hash)` and `may_contain(edge_hash)` operations.
4. On `may_contain() == true`: verify with exact edge comparison (handle false positives).
5. Replace `HashSet<(NodeId, NodeId)>` in parser with `QuotientFilter` for WASM target.
6. Keep `HashSet` for native target (simpler, negligible space overhead).
7. Benchmark: memory usage and parse time for 1000, 10000, 100000 edge graphs on WASM.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] QuotientFilter implementation with configurable false positive rate
- [ ] Duplicate edge detection correct (no false negatives, false positives handled)
- [ ] Memory reduction >= 10x vs HashSet for 10000-edge graphs
- [ ] Parse time comparable to HashSet (within 10%)
- [ ] WASM-specific optimization (cfg-gated)
- [ ] Property test: no false negatives over 100000 random edge sets
- [ ] Decision contract: adopt for WASM if memory reduction > 5x
close_reason: Implemented QuotientFilter in fm-core/src/quotient_filter.rs with: configurable q/r bit widths, FxHash-based fingerprinting, linear probing with sorted runs, insert/may_contain O(1) amortized operations, with_capacity auto-sizing (75% load target), memory/FP rate introspection. 14 unit tests all passing: basic operations, duplicates, edge tuples, stress testing (1000 elements, zero false negatives), empirical FP rate verification, memory comparison vs HashSet. All quality gates pass (check, clippy, fmt).

title: Implement class relationship cardinality and namespace grouping
description:
# Class Cardinality and Namespace Grouping

## What mermaid-js Supports
\`\`\`
classDiagram
  namespace Animals {
    class Dog
    class Cat
  }
  Dog "1" --> "*" Cat : chases
  Vehicle "1" *-- "0..*" Wheel
\`\`\`
- Cardinality labels: "1", "*", "0..1", "1..*", "0..*" on relationship ends
- Namespace blocks group classes visually (like packages in UML)
- Relationship types: inheritance (<|--), composition (*--), aggregation (o--), association (-->), dependency (..>), realization (..|>)

## Current State
- Cardinality labels on relationships: NOT parsed
- Namespace blocks: NOT parsed
- All relationship arrow types ARE parsed

## Implementation Plan
1. **Parser**: Parse quoted cardinality labels before/after relationship arrows. Parse \`namespace Name { ... }\` blocks as clusters.
2. **IR**: Add source_cardinality/target_cardinality: Option<String> to IrEdge. Namespaces map to IrCluster.
3. **SVG Renderer**: Render cardinality labels near edge endpoints. Render namespaces as labeled boundary boxes.
4. **Tests**: Various cardinality labels, namespace grouping, nested namespaces.

title: Sugiyama edge anchors use box side midpoints, which fall outside triangle/trapezoid/parallelogram outlines
description:
Same defect CLASS as bd-kaxw (closed, fixed) but on the MAIN Sugiyama path, so the blast radius and the golden cost are much larger. Filed with evidence rather than fixed, because the fix moves emitted geometry for every diagram using these shapes and that is a GOLDEN-CHANGE decision, not a drive-by.

MECHANISM. edge_anchors (crates/fm-layout/src/lib.rs:13896) attaches every edge at a BOX SIDE MIDPOINT: for horizontal ranks, (bounds.x + width, centre.y) on the source and (bounds.x, centre.y) on the target; vertical ranks use the top/bottom midpoints. That is exactly right for shapes inscribed touching their box at side midpoints — Rect, Rounded, Circle, Diamond — which is why this went unnoticed and why the Sugiyama path was correctly ruled OUT of bd-kaxw.

It is wrong for shapes that do not. VERIFIED against the renderer's own path, crates/fm-render-svg/src/lib.rs:9008: a Triangle is drawn apex-top at (cx, y) with base corners (x, y+h) and (x+w, y+h). At the vertical midpoint y + h/2 the triangle spans only x + w/4 .. x + 3w/4, so the left and right side midpoints that edge_anchors uses sit w/4 — a full 25% of the node width — OUTSIDE the drawn shape. In an LR or RL flowchart the arrowhead floats in empty space beside the triangle.

DIRECTION-DEPENDENT, which is worth knowing before anyone 'fixes' it globally: for a Triangle, TD/BT is already CORRECT because the apex is at top-centre and the base is flat, so the top and bottom midpoints do lie on the outline. Only the horizontal anchors are wrong. A shape-aware anchor must therefore be computed per side, not per shape.

LIKELY ALSO AFFECTED, not individually verified — check each against its renderer path before acting: Trapezoid, InvTrapezoid, Parallelogram, InvParallelogram, Pentagon, Star, Cloud, Tag, Hexagon. Hexagon and Stadium may be fine or nearly so depending on how far their outline is inset at the midpoint; do not assume.

WHY THIS IS NOT JUST COSMETIC: cross-engine output equivalence is part of the ratio in this repo, and mermaid-js terminates edges on the drawn outline. An edge that visibly misses its node is a fidelity loss, and per AGENTS.md a renderer that mislays an edge is not faster, it is wrong.

REQUIRED APPROACH:
1. Decide the contract first: does an anchor sit on the OUTLINE, or on the box with the renderer responsible for hiding the gap? bd-kaxw chose the outline for the force path; the two paths should agree.
2. Per-side, per-shape anchor geometry — not a single 'shape radius'. Reuse the approach from clip_to_shape_border (lib.rs, added in cf2dd848): exact analytic outlines for shapes where the box is clearly wrong, box fallback otherwise, so shapes nobody has reported wrong do not move.
3. Expect goldens to move. Every changed golden needs a semantic diff explaining which edge endpoint moved, by how much, and why the new position is the more correct one — never a bulk refresh.
4. Test the HELPER with a guaranteed diagonal/side-on approach, not an end-to-end layout. bd-kaxw's first test passed while exercising nothing because two force nodes settle axis-aligned; a layout-level test of a geometry bug can silently avoid the geometry.
5. Negative controls: Rect must still anchor at the box, and Circle/Diamond must be UNCHANGED by this work, since they are already correct — that is what proves the change is targeted rather than a global shift.
close_reason:
Fixed in c84da534.

DEFECT: edge_anchors attached every edge at a bounding-box side midpoint. Correct for Rect/Rounded/Circle/Diamond/Hexagon/Stadium, which touch their box there — that is why the Sugiyama path was correctly ruled OUT of bd-kaxw — but wrong for shapes whose sides slant away from the box between the horizontal edges.

VERIFIED against the renderers' own paths rather than assumed:
  Triangle (fm-render-svg lib.rs:9008): apex (cx, y) over a full-width base, so at mid-height it spans only x+w/4..x+3w/4. The side anchor floated a QUARTER of the node width outside the drawn shape in LR/RL.
  Trapezoid / InvTrapezoid / Parallelogram / InvParallelogram: slant by SLANTED_SHAPE_INSET_RATIO (0.15w) across full height, so half is gone by mid-height => 7.5% of width.

PER-DIRECTION, as the bead required: vertical anchors are untouched and were already correct (a triangle's apex is at top-centre, its base spans the full width). The inset is reported for the horizontal direction only.

CONTRACT (bead step 1): anchors sit on the OUTLINE, matching the choice bd-kaxw made for the force path. The two paths now agree.

PLACEMENT: the ratio is a method on NodeShape in fm-core, beside the shape it describes and beside the slant constant, so layout agrees with what is drawn. NOTE FOR FOLLOW-UP: crates/fm-render-svg/src/lib.rs still hardcodes 0.15 at BOTH of its draw sites (~7559 and ~8960); they should adopt fm_core::SLANTED_SHAPE_INSET_RATIO so the constant cannot drift between drawing and anchoring. Not done here to keep this change to one concern.

SHAPES DELIBERATELY LEFT ALONE: Hexagon, Stadium, Asymmetric, Pentagon, Star, Cloud, Tag. They are either correct or unverified, and Hexagon/Stadium/Asymmetric are the ones the golden corpus actually exercises. Guessing at them would move goldens to fix shapes nobody has reported wrong. The bead's 'likely also affected' list is therefore only partly consumed — Pentagon/Star/Cloud/Tag remain unverified and unfixed.

title: Parse and render sequence diagram notes
description:
# Sequence Diagram Notes ## What mermaid-js Supports \`\`\` sequenceDiagram Note left of Alice: Single line note Note right of Bob: Another note Note over Alice,Bob: Spanning note Note over Alice: Multi-line

Position note boxes at the appropriate x (left/right/over participant) and y (between messages). 4. **SVG Renderer**: Draw note boxes with folded corner (small triangle in top-right). Add text with word wrapping. 5. **Tests**: Left note, right note, over single, over span, multi-line.
