title: CI quality gates cannot run: 17 sites use 'cargo -p fm-cli', which is a BINARY name, not the package
description:
FALSE-GREEN GATE FAMILY, and it disables five gates that are all switched ON.

MEASURED. The package in crates/fm-cli/Cargo.toml is named frankenmermaid-cli. 'fm-cli' is one of its three BINARY targets, not a package. So every CI invocation spelled 'cargo ... -p fm-cli' fails before it does any work:

  $ cargo test -p fm-cli --test golden_svg_test --no-run
  error: package ID specification `fm-cli` did not match any packages

There are 17 such sites in .github/workflows/ci.yml, plus the same mistake inside .ci/quality-gates.toml which supplies commands to the workflow:

  ci.yml:234  cargo test -p fm-cli --test golden_svg_test              (golden-checksum-guard)
  ci.yml:237  cargo test -p fm-cli --test golden_layout_test           (golden-checksum-guard)
  ci.yml:307  cargo test -p fm-cli --test integration_test e2e_pipeline_determinism_all_types
  ci.yml:333  cargo run  -p fm-cli -- determinism-manifest
  ci.yml:362  cargo build -p fm-cli --target wasm32-wasip1
  ci.yml:183/186  cargo check/test -p fm-cli --features png            (png-smoke)
  ci.yml:491,569,575,587,600,607,609,633,658,717  evidence-ledger-guard and friends
  quality-gates.toml:33  cargo test -p fm-cli --test invariant_proof_harness   (invariant_proof.command)
  quality-gates.toml:47  cargo test -p fm-cli --test golden_layout_test layout_golden_cases_are_deterministic_across_runs  (determinism.command)
  quality-gates.toml:57  cargo test -p fm-cli --test invariant_proof_harness deg_   (degradation.command)

EVERY GATE IS ENABLED, so this is not dormant configuration. .ci/quality-gates.toml has enabled = true for golden_checksum, performance_regression, property_test, invariant_proof, evidence_ledger, determinism, decision_contract, degradation, release_gate_overrides, release_signoff, demo_evidence. The jobs exist with real bodies and real steps. They simply cannot execute the check they are named for.

THE TARGETS ALL EXIST AND ALL PASS, which is what makes this purely a spelling defect rather than missing work. With the package spelled correctly:
  cargo test -p frankenmermaid-cli --test invariant_proof_harness --no-run   -> builds
  cargo test -p frankenmermaid-cli --test integration_test e2e_pipeline_determinism_all_types -> 1 passed
crates/fm-cli/tests/ contains golden_svg_test.rs, golden_layout_test.rs, integration_test.rs and invariant_proof_harness.rs. Nothing is missing; the gates were pointing at a name that does not resolve.

SECOND, COUPLED DEFECT — correcting the package name alone is NOT sufficient. The package declares three binaries (frankenmermaid, fm-cli, evidence) and has NO default-run key, so the sites of the form 'cargo run -p <pkg> -- determinism-manifest' become ambiguous the moment the package resolves:

  $ cargo run -p frankenmermaid-cli -- --help
  error: `cargo run` could not determine which binary to run. Use the `--bin` option to specify a binary, or the `default-run` manifest key.
  available binaries: evidence, fm-cli, frankenmermaid

So the fix is two-part: correct the package spec everywhere, AND make the bare 'cargo run' sites unambiguous (add default-run = "fm-cli" to crates/fm-cli/Cargo.toml, which is the mechanism cargo's own error recommends, or pass --bin explicitly at each site). Landing only the first half converts a resolve failure into an ambiguity failure.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR bd-17e4.5, which is what led me here: that bead asks for six CI gates and every one of them ALREADY EXISTS as a named job — golden-checksum-guard, performance-regression-guard, property-test-guard, evidence-ledger-guard, determinism-guard, decision-contract-guard, plus extras (invariant-proof-guard, degradation-guard, cross-platform-determinism-native/wasm/compare, release-gate-override-guard, demo-evidence-guard, quality-summary, ledger-integrity-guard). The bead is not unimplemented; its deliverable is implemented and BROKEN. It should be re-scoped to this defect rather than re-implemented.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA, observable:
1. Every 'cargo ... -p <spec>' in .github/workflows/ci.yml and .ci/quality-gates.toml names a package that 'cargo metadata' actually lists. Worth asserting mechanically, since this is the second time a gate has been trusted without being run (see the false-green note below).
2. Each corrected command RUNS — verified by executing it locally, not by reading it.
3. No 'cargo run -p ...' without an unambiguous binary.
4. The correction does not silently change which tests run: the referenced test names must match existing targets.

WHY IT WENT UNNOTICED, for the record: a job that fails at 'package ID specification did not match any packages' fails fast and identically regardless of the code under test, so it produces the same red on every commit and stops carrying information. This is the same family as the documented `cargo check --all-targets` without --workspace incident, where main sat red for six hours under green claims. A gate that cannot fail differently is not a gate.

NOT INVESTIGATED, deliberately: whether CI has actually been red on these jobs, or whether something upstream marks them non-blocking. I have no CI run history here, only the workflow definition. Either answer makes the fix necessary; the difference only changes how long it has been broken.

ALSO NOTICED, not filed: crates/fm-cli declares two binaries (frankenmermaid, fm-cli) from the SAME src/main.rs, which cargo warns about on every single build ('file ... found to be present in multiple build targets'). Cosmetic, unrelated to this defect, and I have not established which of the two is intended to be canonical.
close_reason:
Fixed by b363bdba, all three parts together.

1. Package spec corrected at all 21 sites (17 in ci.yml, 4 in .ci/quality-gates.toml): -p fm-cli -> -p frankenmermaid-cli.
2. default-run = "frankenmermaid" added to crates/fm-cli/Cargo.toml, because correcting the package alone converts the resolve failure into an AMBIGUITY failure at the bare 'cargo run -p ... -- determinism-manifest' sites (three binaries, no default). Points at the canonical binary, not the transitional fm-cli alias.
3. 'set -euo pipefail' added to the five gate steps that pipe into tee. This is the part that makes 1 and 2 into a gate rather than a decoration.

VERIFIED BY EXECUTION, which was acceptance criterion 2 — every command from the config run for real, exit codes captured with no pipe in the way:
  EXIT=0  invariant_proof.command                 12 passed
  EXIT=0  determinism.command                      1 passed
  EXIT=0  degradation.command                      3 passed
  EXIT=0  performance_regression cmd[0] fm-layout 11 passed
  EXIT=0  performance_regression cmd[1] perf_slo_  6 passed
  EXIT=0  ci.yml golden_svg_test                   8 passed
  EXIT=0  ci.yml golden_layout_test                2 passed
Every one previously exited non-zero on the package spec.

CONTROL for the pipefail half, measured not reasoned:
  bash -e            -c 'false | tee /dev/null'  -> EXIT=0  (masked)
  bash -e + pipefail -c 'false | tee /dev/null'  -> EXIT=1  (surfaced)
GitHub Actions' default shell is 'bash -e {0}', so -e alone could not have saved these steps.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERION 1, the mechanical check, done and worth keeping: every 'cargo ... -p <spec>' in both files is cross-checked against cargo metadata's package names -> NONE unresolved. The probe asserts it found >= 5 packages BEFORE judging, because my first version silently received an empty package list and reported every spec as broken. A check that can degrade into a meaningless verdict is the same bug class as the one this bead fixes; I did not want to ship that shape while fixing this shape.

CRITERION 3: no 'cargo run -p ...' without an unambiguous binary — satisfied via default-run; 'cargo run -p frankenmermaid-cli -- determinism-manifest' now emits its JSON manifest instead of erroring.
CRITERION 4: the referenced test targets all exist (golden_svg_test.rs, golden_layout_test.rs, integration_test.rs, invariant_proof_harness.rs) and the corrected commands select real tests, as the pass counts above show. Nothing silently changed which tests run.

ONE PIPE DELIBERATELY LEFT: ci.yml:795 'find ... | sort | tail -n 1' inside a command substitution PICKS A FILENAME and judges nothing by exit status. Correct as written; recorded so a future sweep does not 'fix' it. It is the only status-masking-looking pipeline left in the file and it is benign.

NOT VERIFIED EITHER WAY, and not claimed: 'cargo build -p frankenmermaid-cli --target wasm32-wasip1' (ci.yml:365). Its package now resolves, but it fails on THIS host with 'can t find crate for std ... the wasm32-wasip1 target may not be installed' — rustup here has wasm32-unknown-unknown but not wasip1, while CI installs it via dtolnay/rust-toolchain@nightly with 'targets: wasm32-wasip1'. So the spelling is fixed and the build outcome is untested by me. Not filed as a defect, because I have no evidence it fails anywhere the target exists.

NOT INVESTIGATED, as stated in the filing: whether CI was actually red on these jobs or something upstream marked them non-blocking. No CI run history is available to me. Either answer made the fix necessary.

ALSO STILL TRUE, not actioned: crates/fm-cli declares two binaries (frankenmermaid, fm-cli) from the SAME src/main.rs, which cargo warns about on every build. The Cargo.toml comment calls fm-cli a backwards-compatibility alias 'during transition', and repo policy says we do not keep compatibility shims — so removing it is probably right, but it changes the shipped binary set and ci.yml:368 consumes target/wasm32-wasip1/debug/fm-cli.wasm by name. Out of scope here; needs its own bead if anyone wants it.

GATES: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings clean (rch remote); cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast EXIT=0 with 40/40 suites green; ci.yml still parses as YAML with 22 jobs; no source file touched so no golden can move. Pushed to main and master at b363bdba.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
SECOND MECHANISM FOUND, and it is why this went unnoticed. Folding it into this bead rather than filing separately because fixing either defect alone leaves the gates still not gating.

FIVE CI GATE STEPS PIPE THEIR GATE COMMAND INTO tee WITH NO pipefail IN SCOPE, so the step's exit status is tee's — effectively always 0 — and the harness's failure is discarded:

  ci.yml:274/279  'Run invariant proof harness'                 ... | tee artifacts/evidence/slo/invariant-proof.log
  ci.yml:521/526  'Run degradation SLO harness'                  ... | tee artifacts/evidence/slo/degradation.log
  ci.yml:565/570  'Capture SVG golden evidence log'              ... | tee artifacts/evidence/logs/svg-golden.log
  ci.yml:572/576  'Capture layout golden evidence log'           ... | tee artifacts/evidence/logs/layout-golden.log
  ci.yml:578/582  'Capture determinism evidence log'             ... | tee artifacts/evidence/logs/determinism.log

Determined mechanically, not by eye: for each '- name:' step I checked whether its run block contains 'pipefail' and whether it contains a pipe into tee/tail/head. These five have the pipe and not the guard. GitHub Actions' default shell is 'bash -e {0}', which does NOT enable pipefail, so -e cannot save them — the pipeline as a whole succeeded. Note ci.yml DOES use 'set -euo pipefail' in other steps (lines 134, 155), so the idiom is known in this file; these five just missed it.

ONE MORE PIPE, CHECKED AND BENIGN: ci.yml:788-789 use '| sort | tail -n 1' inside a command substitution to PICK A FILENAME. Judging nothing by its status, so it is correct as written. Recording it so a future sweep does not 'fix' it.

THE TWO DEFECTS COMPOUND, which is the actual story here. 'cargo test -p fm-cli ...' fails immediately with 'package ID specification fm-cli did not match any packages'; the tee then reports success. So these gates have been REPORTING GREEN WHILE EXECUTING NOTHING. That is strictly worse than a red gate: a red gate gets fixed. This is the same family as the documented 'cargo check --all-targets without --workspace' incident.

FIX MUST BE ALL THREE PARTS TOGETHER or the gate stays broken:
  1. package spec: -p fm-cli -> -p frankenmermaid-cli (17 sites in ci.yml, 3 command strings in .ci/quality-gates.toml)
  2. bare 'cargo run -p ... --' sites need an unambiguous binary (default-run = "fm-cli" in crates/fm-cli/Cargo.toml)
  3. 'set -euo pipefail' in the five steps above, so a failing harness fails its step

Part 3 is the one that turns the other two into a gate rather than a decoration. Landing 1+2 without 3 would make the commands run but still swallow their verdict.

title: Deeply nested mindmap input overflows the stack and aborts the process
description:
Found by cc lane (LilacPike) while establishing whether a failing test was pre-existing.

crates/fm-cli/tests/test_tree_overflow.rs builds a mindmap with 10,000 levels of nesting (each line
indented two more spaces) and calls fm_parser::parse then fm_layout::layout_diagram. Result:

  thread 'test_tree_overflow' has overflowed its stack
  fatal runtime error: stack overflow, aborting
  process didn't exit successfully (signal: 6, SIGABRT)

So a deep-but-small text input does not produce a diagnostic or a bounded error -- it ABORTS the
process. For a library that renders untrusted markup this is a robustness/DoS concern, not just a
failing test: no amount of caller error handling can catch a stack overflow abort.

PRE-EXISTING, not from this session's parser work. Two independent reasons:
1. It appeared identically in test runs at base 77c3a091 and earlier, before the inheritance change.
2. This session's edits are ArrowType/MarkerKind variants, marker dispatch, a11y phrase strings, and
   the state colon-label split. None touches mindmap parsing or tree-layout recursion. ArrowType grew
   from 31 to 37 variants, which stays a one-byte discriminant, so there is no struct-size change that
   could tip a borderline stack frame.

Note the test itself has NO assertions -- it parses, lays out, and prints timings. It looks like a
manual reproduction harness committed as a test, so it has presumably been red for a long time and
its failure is easy to dismiss as noise. It is not noise; it is an unbounded-recursion abort.

WANTED: a depth limit in the mindmap/tree path that returns a Diagnostic (the repo already bounds
input SIZE via core.max_input_bytes, cf. 894fdc1f, but not input DEPTH), or an explicitly heap-based
traversal. Then either give this test a real assertion or move it to the fuzz corpus.
close_reason:
Fixed: ParserConfig.max_nesting_depth (default 256) bounds recursive-descent nesting in parse_flowchart_document_items and parse_block_beta_document_items; surplus levels are flattened into the deepest accepted container with a warning, preserving nodes/edges and keeping end-matching balanced.

DIAGNOSIS CORRECTION: the bead named the mindmap/tree path. That case no longer aborts (verified: 10k-level mindmap parses + lays out in 3.0s; layout tree helpers compute_tree_subtree_spans/compute_all_tree_span_centers are already explicit-stack/BFS). The live unbounded recursion was the FLOWCHART subgraph document parser, plus the same pattern in block-beta.

REPRODUCTION (pre-fix, debug fm-cli): gdb backtrace on 50k nested 'subgraph' = 2965/3000 frames in fm_parser::mermaid_parser::parse_flowchart_document_items -> SIGSEGV. Depth bisect: subgraph ok@2000 FAIL@4000; block-beta ok@4000 FAIL@8000. Input was 966 KB -- well under core.max_input_bytes=5000000, and that limit is CLI-only, so the library API was fully exposed. Nesting is NOT bounded by input size: unindented 'subgraph S/end' costs ~14 bytes per level.

title: Update README FNX section to honestly reflect current integration status
description:
## Problem
README Section "Optional FNX Integration" describes FNX (franken_networkx) as if it's a simple optional feature flag you can toggle on. In reality:
- There are ~25 open P1 beads under the bd-ml2r epic covering architecture, adapter, diagnostics, cycle scoring, ordering enrichment, telemetry, runtime budgets, UX controls, comprehensive verification, and rollout.
- Only 2 of those 25 beads are in-progress (bd-ml2r.1 and bd-ml2r.1.1 — the very first sub-tasks).
- The feature flags exist in Cargo.toml but the actual integration code is not yet written.

This is the project's most ambitious unfinished initiative, and the README makes it sound like a toggle.

## Fix
Update the README FNX section to:
1. Keep the existing Cargo feature flag documentation (it's accurate for the BUILD story).
2. Add a clear status note: "FNX integration is currently in early development. The feature flags compile but the integration surface is not yet functional. See the project's issue tracker for the bd-ml2r epic tracking this work."
3. Optionally add a brief roadmap: Phase 1 (undirected graph intelligence + diagnostics) → Phase 2 (directed graph analysis + ordering enrichment).

## Why This Matters
Understating the gap between "feature flag exists" and "feature works" is a soft form of README dishonesty. Users or contributors who enable `--features fnx-integration` and find it does nothing will lose trust. Honest disclosure costs nothing and builds credibility.

## Acceptance Criteria
- README FNX section includes honest status disclosure.
- No false impression that enabling the feature flag gives you working functionality.
- Roadmap or link to issue tracker for follow-up.
close_reason: Added honest status disclosure (early development, feature flags compile but not functional), roadmap (Phase 1/2), and link to FNX_INTEGRATION.md ADR.

title: Decide: build a real CGA meet()/join() operator, or reword bd-2q3f criteria around the analytic queries
description:
bd-2q3f (EPIC: Geometric/Conformal Algebra for Transforms) and its children are written as if CGA meet/join operators exist and are being adopted. THEY DO NOT EXIST. Verified 2026-08-04: there is no meet(), join(), regressive product, or outer-product-of-points anywhere in crates/fm-core/src/cga.rs.

What actually exists:
- CgaPoint / CgaLineSegment / CgaCircle / CgaRect as plain Euclidean structs
- Multivector + geometric_product + to_multivector (a real conformal embedding), used ONLY by inner_product
- All intersection queries (segment/segment, circle/segment, circle/circle, rect/segment) implemented ANALYTICALLY via parametric and quadratic solutions, not via meet

This matters beyond naming, because the one place the conformal embedding WAS load-bearing turned out to be a defect: distance measured d^2 = -2 P.Q through the embedding, which squares coordinates before subtracting, and for points ~90 from the origin resolved a true 1e-9 separation as EXACTLY 0.0. Fixed in 681cdf4a by measuring directly. So the evidence so far is that the conformal route is numerically WORSE than the analytic one for the operations this engine actually performs.

DECIDE ONE:
(a) Build meet()/join() properly, and justify it against that evidence -- what does it buy that the analytic queries do not? Degenerate-case uniformity is the usual argument; it must be demonstrated, not asserted, and priced (bd-2q3f.4 exists for the perf/decision contract).
(b) Declare the analytic implementations the intended endpoint and REWORD bd-2q3f.3 criteria 1-3 accordingly, so nobody later reads 'meet operation correct for line-line' as an unmet requirement or quietly marks it met by pointing at analytic code.

DO NOT let this resolve by drift. Criterion 1 has already been satisfied in the (b) sense (intersection queries verified against their geometric definition, 681cdf4a) while the criterion text still says 'meet operation'. Blocks a coherent reading of bd-2q3f.3 and bd-zace.
close_reason:
DECIDED: option (b). The analytic implementations are the intended endpoint. Do NOT build meet()/join() for this engine's paths. Decided on measurement, not preference — bench landed in 630a4f34, crates/fm-layout/benches/cga_transforms.rs.

=== DECISION CONTRACT ===

EVIDENCE 1 — CGA transforms cost 10-40x more than the matrices they would replace. Criterion, per-iteration, same invocation, non-overlapping CIs, ELF 82c691cee9869c791cfabd8c8dc52c6edcdebe15c7d75c6cb7ae2057a7c734c2 self-reported from inside the process:
  compose x4    61.2 ns -> 2.13 us   (34.8x)
  compose x16  235.9 ns -> 9.34 us   (39.6x)
  compose x64   1.01 us -> 38.49 us  (38.1x)
  compose+apply 1024 pts  973 ns -> 9.94 us (10.2x)
bd-2q3f.4's own complexity table predicted ~2.4x. Measured is ~15x worse than that prediction because Rotor::compose does not multiply rotors — it round-trips through a full 16-component Multivector::geometric_product (256 component products) and never exploits the even subalgebra. callgrind puts 12.19% of the rotor arm in geometric_product alone.

EVIDENCE 2 — where conformal machinery WAS load-bearing, it was numerically wrong. CgaPoint::distance evaluated d^2 = -2 P.Q through the embedding, which squares coordinates before subtracting. For points ~90 from the origin a true separation of 1e-9 came back as EXACTLY 0.0, and a point that intersect_segment had just placed ON a segment measured 2^-14 off it. Replaced with the direct form in 681cdf4a. So the one measured instance of 'use the conformal identity' made results WORSE, not more robust.

EVIDENCE 3 — the abstraction is not present anyway. There is no meet(), join(), regressive product, or outer-product-of-points in cga.rs. Every intersection query (segment/segment, circle/segment, circle/circle, rect/segment) is analytic. Adopting meet would be new construction, not migration.

WHAT IS FAIR TO THE CGA SIDE: the 35-40x is against THIS rotor implementation. An optimized 8-component even-subalgebra compose would land far closer to the predicted 2.4x. The decision does not rest on the bad implementation alone — it rests on the fact that even at its theoretical best it is slower than what it replaces, and the only measured quality argument in its favour (conditioning) went the other way. CGA's real advantages, uniform handling of degenerate cases and coordinate-free composition, are not free here: the analytic code already handles its degenerate cases (verified by the 20k-case sweep in 5f62bb80 and the definition-based checks in 681cdf4a).

CONSEQUENCES, to be applied by whoever owns those beads:
1. bd-2q3f.3 criteria 1-3 should be REWORDED from 'meet operation correct for X' to 'intersection queries verified correct for X'. Criterion 1 is already satisfied in that sense (681cdf4a) and criterion 3 already holds (fm-wasm uses CgaRect::contains and CgaLineSegment::distance_to_point). Leaving the current wording invites a future agent to either build meet unnecessarily or quietly mark it met by pointing at analytic code.
2. bd-zace (edge-routing boundary clipping, blocked on this) is UNBLOCKED and its framing resolves to the second of the two it names: consolidate duplicated clipping arithmetic onto the shared fm-core primitives. Not 'adopt CGA meet'.
3. bd-2q3f.4 can be answered from this bench rather than re-run; it is currently blocked behind bd-17e4.1/.3 and bd-2q3f.2/.3.
4. Rotor/Multivector are NOT to be deleted — they are used by to_affine_matrix and the transform stack, and bd-2q3f.2 is in progress on that surface. This decision is about not EXTENDING the abstraction, not about removing what exists.

RETRY PREDICATE: revisit only if someone implements an even-subalgebra rotor compose and measures it within 3x of the matrix path AND demonstrates a degenerate case the analytic queries get wrong that meet gets right.

SUBSTRATE FINDING — perf is DEAD on this host, and the fleet's 'PMU alive' note is stale.

/proc/sys/kernel/perf_event_paranoid = 4. That is stricter than the documented ladder: >=1 already disallows CPU event access, so BOTH 'perf record' (even with a user-space-only event like cpu-clock:u) and 'perf stat -e instructions' fail with 'Access to performance monitoring and observability operations is limited'. perf stat -e task-clock fails too. SUBSTITUTE: valgrind 3.25.1 + callgrind_annotate are installed. Callgrind Ir counts are deterministic and load-INDEPENDENT, which is strictly better than perf for this repo's contract: the ledger's '**Counted mechanism:** instructions ...' marker is satisfiable, and the A/A null is trivially exact rather than statistical. Cost is ~50-100x slowdown, so use criterion --profile-time 1 and compare two separately-built ELFs rather than long runs.

    --config profile.release.lto=false --config profile.bench.strip=false \

comments.author: PeachGorge
comments.text:
⚠️ RETRACTION — the '-4.074% instructions' figure on this bead is METHOD-INVALID and must not be quoted or ledgered. Found while trying to write the PERF_LEDGER KEEP row that bd-x3zl's ELF self-report finally unblocked. The LEVER IS STILL REAL; the number is not.

WHAT WAS WRONG. Both arms were measured as callgrind TOTAL Ir under 'criterion --profile-time 1'. profile-time runs each arm for a fixed WALL second, and under callgrind wall time is dominated by simulation cost, which is itself proportional to instructions executed. So a cheaper arm simply completes MORE iterations in the same second and the total lands in the same place: the metric answers 'how much work fits in a second', not 'what does one edit cost'. I identified this exact trap earlier in the session while measuring rotor-vs-matrix and then failed to apply it to my own result here.

TWO INDEPENDENT PROOFS the metric is not measuring the lever:
1. Re-measured today with self-reporting ELFs, same command, same two arms: two-walk 3,038,095,487 Ir vs fused 3,026,115,751 Ir = -0.054%. Meanwhile per-iteration wall for those SAME binaries differs by 2.4-4.3%. The metric is insensitive to an effect that is plainly there.
2. The same command on the same code gave ~331,360,000 total Ir originally and ~3,038,000,000 today — a 9x swing driven by machine conditions, not by code.

WHAT THE LEVER ACTUALLY MEASURES, by a method that accounts for iterations. Criterion per-iteration, two counterbalanced passes, self-reported ELFs cb674015... (two-walk) and fc89a91a... (fused), which are distinct so this is not a build compared against itself:
  pass 1  two-walk [148.01, 149.18, 150.70] us   fused [143.84, 145.63, 148.08] us   -2.38%
  pass 2  two-walk [150.31, 151.83, 153.20] us   fused [143.94, 145.31, 146.63] us   -4.29%  (CIs disjoint)
Direction is consistent and the mechanism is sound — one walk instead of two over the same node ids and Vec<String> membership — so 83a94342 STAYS. It is a real improvement of roughly 2-4% on this row, not the 4.074% instruction reduction claimed.

NO KEEP ROW WRITTEN, and this is why. docs/PERF_LEDGER.md requires a same-invocation A/A null OR a counted mechanism. I have neither in conforming form: the counted mechanism is the invalid total-Ir above, and the wall numbers come from separate invocations on a host at load 6-10. Writing the row from the retracted figure would be exactly the proof-class inflation the contract exists to stop, and writing it from the wall numbers would misrepresent separate invocations as a same-invocation gate.

WHAT WOULD MAKE IT LEDGERABLE: a FIXED-ITERATION harness — run N identical edits under callgrind with N pinned, so total Ir divides cleanly by N and is comparable across arms. criterion's profile-time cannot provide that. Filed as bd-3mxu.

FLEET-WIDE WARNING: any result in this repo measured as callgrind total Ir under criterion --profile-time is suspect for the same reason. The substrate note I left on this bead earlier recommended exactly that method; treat that recommendation as withdrawn.

comments.author: PeachGorge
comments.text:
LEDGER ROW WRITTEN — 4c7086ef, docs/PERF_LEDGER.md:L3849 — at the RE-DERIVED figure, not the retracted one. The deferral recorded in my previous comment is now lifted.

FINAL NUMBER: -0.610% instructions per edit, an order of magnitude smaller than the -4.074% this bead carried. baseline 15,422,061.6 Ir/edit, candidate 15,328,041.3, 94,020 removed per edit.

HOW IT IS NOW SOUND, point by point against what was wrong before:
- Per-edit, not per-wall-second. The fixed-iteration harness (bd-3m9p, landed b00f77d1) runs exactly N edits with N pinned by the caller and no wall clock in the loop, so total Ir / N is comparable across arms. The old method let a cheaper arm complete more iterations inside the same wall window, which is why it was blind to the effect.
- Divisor is PRINTED by the process (fixed_iterations=200), so the artifact carries what it divided by.
- A/A null EXACTLY 1.000000000 on both arms: the same ELF twice returns byte-identical Ir (3,084,412,314 twice; 3,065,608,265 twice). Callgrind is simulated, so this is an identity check, not a statistical one.
- Self-reported ELFs 95f5e41b... (baseline) and fa08389b... (fused), read from each process's own bench_elf_sha256= line rather than hashed beside the run, and DISTINCT — so this is not a build compared against itself.
- Labelled INTRA-REPO / maintenance-self-speedup in the row: two frankenmermaid builds, nothing about mermaid-js, never to be quoted as a competitive ratio.
- Passes the contract gate: ledger_preflight --lint --staged accepts it.

WALL AND INSTRUCTIONS DISAGREE, and both are in the row rather than just the flattering one. Wall is -2.4% and -4.3% (CIs disjoint in pass 2) against -0.610% instructions. That is coherent, not contradictory: the walk this lever deletes is memcmp over node-id and Vec<String> membership, so removing it buys more in memory traffic than in instruction count, and instructions are blind to cache. The honest summary is 'small instruction win, larger wall win, mechanism explains the gap'.

THE LEVER STANDS. 83a94342 is kept — the mechanism is sound and both metrics point the same direction. Only the magnitude was wrong.

The retraction and both proofs that the old metric measures nothing are recorded IN THE LEDGER ROW itself, not just here, so the mistake is discoverable from the ledger by someone who never reads this bead.

So the blast radius is exactly ONE claim: mine, already retracted and re-derived at -0.610%. No other lane needs to re-derive anything.

Recording it here so the over-broad version is not quoted from my earlier comment.

STILL TRUE AND UNCHANGED: the metric itself is invalid for cross-arm comparison, the fixed-iteration harness (bd-3m9p) is the fix, and only incremental_layout has it — crossing_minimization and barycenter_sweep would each need it before any instruction claim on them is comparable.

title: reorder_rank_by_barycenter is 47.64% of pipeline on Sugiyama diagrams; the 4 prior rejections benched dead code
description:
SUBSTRATE DEFECT FOUND + LEVER LICENSED. Full write-up: .benchmarks/crossing_min_rejections_benched_dead_code.md

THE FINDING. perf record on the existing symbolized binary, self-time as % of the whole parse+layout+render pipeline:
  wide_8x16   (= layout_wide/8x16)   fm_layout 21.80%   barycenter+total_crossings 0.000%   tree 2.83%
  wide_16x32  (= layout_wide/16x32)  fm_layout 14.16%   barycenter+total_crossings 0.000%   tree 3.66%
  wide_40x80                         fm_layout 10.41%   barycenter+total_crossings 0.000%   tree 3.27%
  cyclic_scc_100 (Sugiyama)          fm_layout 70.76%   barycenter+total_crossings 48.450%  sugiyama 11.17%

bench_layout_wide (pipeline_bench.rs:306) builds inputs with gen_wide() and registers them as BenchmarkId::new('layered', ..). The name says layered; the auto-selector picks TREE. All FOUR rejected rewrites of the barycenter/crossing-counting area (barycenter-sweep-precomputed-edge-adjacency, flat-array-total-crossings-position-edge-tables, dense-crossing-count-position-maps, local-delta crossing_refinement) were A/B'd on layout_wide/{8x16,12x24,16x32} -- three inputs where the code under test executes ZERO instructions. Their outcomes are exactly what that predicts: +1.40% 'No change', +1.70% 'No change', and +5.84% REGRESSED on 16x32 (the adjacency BUILD cost added to a path that never reads it). Not four pieces of evidence that the lever fails -- one piece of evidence that the bench was wrong, repeated four times.

The do-not-retry's escape clause ('do not attempt further container/adjacency rewrites WITHOUT a CPU profile that names the actual dominant function') is now SATISFIED. It names reorder_rank_by_barycenter at 47.64%. It also refutes the note's own nominated candidate: Brandes-Koepf (bk_horizontal_compaction::place_block) is 0.74% -- COLD.

NOTE: the layout bottleneck is DIAGRAM-SHAPE-DEPENDENT. dense_dag_200 routes to Tree: fm_layout 26.44%, find_obstacle_nudge_x alone 19.36%, barycenter 0.000%. No single bench stands in for the crate.

MECHANISM (fm-layout/src/lib.rs:11572). Called ~rounds(4)*2*ranks times per layout. Each call: (a) ordering_by_rank.get(&rank).cloned() = 1 Vec alloc; (b) builds adjacent_position: BTreeMap (alloc + O(k log k)); (c) for ranks narrower than SINGLE_PASS_RANK_THRESHOLD=8 -- the common case (~100 nodes over ~25 ranks => ~4/rank) -- RESCANS THE ENTIRE ir.edges LIST PER NODE, doing a ranks.get(&n) BTreeMap probe per edge. O(rank_size * |E| * log|V|) per call; ~188k B-tree probes per layout.

LEVER (do (1) first):
  1. Dense Vec<u32> rank array built ONCE per crossing_minimization, replacing the innermost BTreeMap probe with an O(1) index. No adjacency built at all. This is a DIFFERENT primitive from the rejected Vec<Vec<usize>> adjacency, whose ~2*node_count outer + node_count inner allocations are exactly what sank it.
  2. Dense Vec<u32> scatter tables reusing ONE scratch buffer for adjacent_position / local_slot instead of per-call BTreeMaps.
  3. Flat CSR incidence (2 allocs, built once) ONLY if (1)-(2) do not suffice.
Output-identical by construction: node_rank[n] == ranks.get(&n).copied().unwrap_or(0); barycenter arithmetic (integer position sum / neighbor count) and the downstream stable sort are untouched.

BLOCKER -- NO BENCH EXERCISES THIS FUNCTION:
 * pipeline_bench::layout_wide -> Tree path, 0.000% barycenter (and the reason 4 rejections are void).
 * fm-layout/benches/crossing_minimization.rs -> benches crossing_min/{sparse_dag,dense_dag,bipartite} over synthetic LayerOrdering/LayerEdges. That is a DIFFERENT crossing minimizer; reorder_rank_by_barycenter takes &MermaidDiagramIr and is never called.
STEP 0 is therefore: add a Sugiyama-routing layout bench. cyclic_scc_100 from scripts/headtohead/corpus.mjs is a known-good generator (cyclic SCC => detect_cycle_components => Sugiyama).

A/B SUBSTRATE (mandatory): rch exec has NO worker-pinning flag and picks workers non-deterministically, so a split-invocation A/B is invalid (see the CORRECTION entry in docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md; RCH_WORKER=hz1 was silently ignored and both arms ran on hz2). Bench ORIG and CAND as two arms of ONE alternating criterion group, in ONE binary, in ONE rch exec invocation -- keep the current reorder_rank_by_barycenter as a bench-only reference fn.

DETERMINISM: golden_layout_test + the layout determinism gate must stay green; add a differential test asserting the dense-rank variant produces byte-identical ordering to the BTreeMap variant across random graphs (same playbook as bd-w5sn's single_pass_scanners_match_per_needle_contains).

title: C4 node box ignores its wrapped description; lines render up to 220px outside the box
description:
THIRD instance of the sizing-ignores-a-diagram-meta class, after bd-4isi (class members truncated) and bd-090g (ER attributes spilled). Found by extending bd-090g's audit to the remaining node metas rather than by inspection.

compute_node_size consults class_meta (via class_compartment_dimensions) and, since bd-090g, node.members. It consults c4_meta NOT AT ALL, so a C4 node box is sized from its label while the renderer draws a type label, a name, and a WRAPPED description inside it.

MEASURED, default config, C4Context with one Person and descriptions of increasing length. Reading the node rect against the fm-c4-description <text> and its <tspan dy=...> stack, no transforms in the document so these are final coordinates:

  desc 'Short'                      lines=1   box y=92.0..158.5  desc 143.8..143.8  overflow 0
  desc ~78 chars                    lines=10  box y=92.0..158.5  desc 150.5..284.6  overflow 131.1px
  desc ~136 chars                   lines=16  box y=92.0..158.5  desc 150.5..374.0  overflow 220.5px

The box height is CONSTANT 66.5 in all three. A 16-line description renders 220px below its own rectangle.

WHY IT HID FROM MY FIRST PASS, worth recording as a probe lesson: the description is ONE <text> element whose y attribute IS inside the box; the lines are <tspan dy="14.90"> children stacking downward from it. A check that reads only the text element's y sees no overflow. Any geometry guard in this family must sum the tspan dy stack.

THE RENDERER ALREADY TRIES TO CONTAIN IT AND CANNOT, which is the interesting part. write_c4_node_into (fm-render-svg lib.rs:7165) computes

  baseline_y = (cursor_y + description_height.min((h * 0.35).max(0.0))).min(y + h - 8.0)

so its author clearly intended the description to stay inside the box. But that clamp applies to the FIRST LINE's baseline only; the tspans then stack downward from wherever it landed, so every subsequent line escapes regardless. Clamping the anchor of a multi-line block does not bound the block. Do not try to fix this by tightening that clamp — it would only pull the first line up while the tail still spills, and pulling it far enough up to fit would push it out of the top.

FIX SHAPE: size the box for the wrapped description in compute_node_size, leaving the renderer alone, exactly as the class and ER siblings do. The circularity is only apparent: compute_node_size already derives width from the label BEFORE height, so it can wrap to that width and then add the line count's height. Renderer geometry to mirror:

  description_font = clamp_font_size(font_size * 0.72, config.min_font_size)
  line_h           = font_size * config.line_height
  available_width  = (w - 20.0).max(32.0)
  lines            = wrap_text_to_lines(description, available_width, config.avg_char_width * 0.92)
  per-line advance = description_font * config.line_height   (this is the tspan dy)

MIND THE ESTIMATOR MISMATCH: the renderer wraps with config.avg_char_width * 0.92 while layout has only metrics. The two need not agree, and UNDER-counting lines under-sizes the box, which is the failure mode being fixed. So layout must round the line count UP — wrap against a slightly narrower effective width, or add a line of margin. Over-sizing renders as padding and is harmless.

ALSO CHECK while fixing: the type label and name rows sit at fixed offsets and fit today, but a very long NAME wraps too (fm-c4-name), so the same tspan-stack question applies to it. I measured only the description.

title: Unreferenced <filter id="node-glow"> emitted on every default render
description:
MEASURED, not inspected. Rendered a plain 3-node flowchart at DEFAULT config via fm-cli render:

  flowchart LR / A-->B / B-->C   ->  8679 bytes
  occurrences of the string 'node-glow' in the output: 1

One. That one is its own definition:

  <filter id="node-glow" x="-50%" y="-50%" width="200%" height="200%"><feDropShadow dx="0" dy="0" stdDeviation="6" flood-opacity="0.35" flood-color="#3b82f6"/></filter>

168 bytes, ~1.9% of that document, referenced by nothing. Control, same binary, same config, with one highlighted node (classDef highlight + class A highlight): 'node-glow' occurs TWICE — def plus filter="url(#node-glow)". So the def is correct when something uses it and is pure dead weight when nothing does.

WHY IT HAPPENS. lib.rs:3677 emits the filter on 'if config.glow_enabled' alone, and glow_enabled DEFAULTS TRUE (lib.rs:252). The only consumer is lib.rs:9239, 'if is_highlighted && config.glow_enabled'. is_highlighted comes solely from a node class matching the 'highlight' keyword (scan_node_class_keywords at 8662, initialised false at 8529 and set nowhere else), which almost no diagram has. So the common case emits the definition and never the reference.

THE SAME FILE ALREADY ESTABLISHES THE CORRECT DOCTRINE, which is why this is a defect and not a preference. The arrowhead-marker block immediately above it (lib.rs:3628) says: 'emit only what the diagram can reference, like Mermaid.js (which never emits unused markers)', and computes emit_fancy_markers by scanning ir.edges first. Sibling <defs> entries in the same builder disagree with each other; the glow filter is the one that did not get the treatment. Note drop-shadow is NOT affected — measured 4 occurrences on the same document, 1 def + 3 references.

FIX SHAPE. Gate the def on the same predicate its consumer uses: config.glow_enabled AND some node in ir.nodes carries a highlight class, computed with scan_node_class_keywords so the two gates cannot drift. The predicate is EXACT, not conservative: ir_node at 8481 is 'ir.nodes.get(node_box.node_index)', so a highlighted node is always an element of ir.nodes, and is_highlighted is false whenever ir_node is None.

THE RISK TO RESPECT, and the reason the gate must mirror rather than approximate: if the def is suppressed while any node still emits filter="url(#node-glow)", the output references a missing filter — invalid SVG and a silently unstyled node, strictly worse than the wasted bytes. A test must cover BOTH directions: no highlight -> no def, highlight -> def AND reference.

ALREADY CHECKED, so nobody re-checks: the streaming fast path render_node_into cannot leak here. Its gate requires node.classes.is_empty() (lib.rs:7998), so a highlighted node can never take it — this is NOT another instance of the fast-path-drops-a-feature family.

EXPECTED GOLDEN IMPACT: probably NONE. golden_svg_test pins glow_enabled: false (golden_svg_test.rs:146), so the fixtures never emit the filter at all. Verify rather than assume; if a golden does move, it needs a GOLDEN-CHANGE note.

PROVENANCE: PeachGorge observed the unreferenced filter while closing bd-ccni and explicitly declined to file it, having seen it in only one configuration. This bead is the confirmation: reproduced at default config, quantified, both directions measured, and the mechanism traced to the two disagreeing gates.
close_reason:
Fixed by 986662f8.

FIX: the <filter id="node-glow"> def is now gated on 'config.glow_enabled && any_node_is_highlighted(ir)', mirroring its consumer's 'is_highlighted && config.glow_enabled' through the SAME scan_node_class_keywords so the def and the reference cannot drift apart.

MEASURED, same command as the filing, default config, flowchart LR / A-->B / B-->C:
  before 8679 bytes, 'node-glow' occurring exactly once (its own def)
  after  8513 bytes, occurring zero times
  delta  exactly 166 bytes; and 'before' with that one filter block excised is BYTE-IDENTICAL to 'after' (checked programmatically, not by eye) so nothing else in the document moved.
Control, same binary, one highlighted node: 'node-glow' occurs twice, def plus filter="url(#node-glow)". The def returns when something can use it.

TESTS (same bead, 2 new; fm-render-svg 277 -> 279):
- glow_filter_def_is_omitted_when_no_node_is_highlighted covers BOTH directions the bead demanded: no highlight => no def; a non-highlight state class => still no def; a highlighted node => def AND reference, so it cannot be satisfied by never emitting glow at all.
- no_defs_entry_is_declared_without_a_reference asserts the GENERAL invariant, because this is the second instance of the class after the marker gating: every id="..." declared inside <defs> must reappear as url(#...) in the document. The next dead def is now a test failure rather than something a byte golden blesses.

NEGATIVE CONTROL: reverting the gate to 'if config.glow_enabled' fails both new tests ('unreferenced glow filter shipped: id="node-glow" ...') while highlighted_node_uses_glow_filter stays green, so the pair discriminates the defect rather than restating the code. File restored byte-identically (diff -q) after the control.

BEAD PREDICTIONS, both confirmed: no golden moved (golden_svg_test pins glow_enabled: false, so the fixtures never emitted the filter -- no bless, no GOLDEN-CHANGE note), and the streaming render_node_into path is NOT another fast-path-drops-a-feature case (its gate requires node.classes.is_empty(), so a highlighted node can never take it).

FOUND WHILE FIXING, recorded not changed: scan_class_keywords_and_clean matches keywords as SUBSTRINGS, so the class 'inactive' contains 'active' and is genuinely treated as highlighted by the renderer. My first test case used 'inactive' as a supposed non-highlight control and correctly failed. The gate mirrors that behaviour rather than second-guessing it, and the test comment names it so a future reader does not misread it as a bug in the gate. Not filed as a separate defect: it is the pre-existing keyword-scan contract, unchanged by this commit, and I have not established that any real class name is misclassified in a way that matters.

LEDGER PREFLIGHT: ran and returned exit 2, matching 'Post-process <style> CSS minification -- REJECTED (render +19%)' (docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md:4208) on the keywords defs/filter. Distinct mechanism and the retry predicate is not engaged: the rejected lever was a post-process reprocessing pass over the CSS, this is a predicate evaluated BEFORE emission and adds no pass. That row's own byte-composition survey explicitly checked the gradient and drop-shadow defs and found them referenced ('so not dead'); it never checked the glow filter. This extends that survey rather than retrying its lever. NO ledger row added: this is an output-correctness fix, not a performance claim, and no timing is asserted anywhere.

title: Parse and render sequence diagram activation/deactivation
description:
# Sequence Activation/Deactivation

## What mermaid-js Supports
\`\`\`
sequenceDiagram
  Alice->>+Bob: Request
  Bob-->>-Alice: Response
  activate Bob
  Bob->>Carol: Forward
  deactivate Bob
\`\`\`
- \`+\` after arrow activates target participant
- \`-\` after arrow deactivates target participant
- \`activate Name\` / \`deactivate Name\` as standalone statements
- Multiple nested activations create stacked boxes
- Activation boxes are narrow rectangles on the lifeline showing active periods

## Current State
- NOT parsed. The +/- modifiers on arrows are ignored.
- No SequenceStatement variant for activate/deactivate.
- Layout does not compute activation box regions.
- SVG renderer does not draw activation boxes.

## Implementation Plan
1. **Parser**: Add SequenceStatement::Activate(String) and Deactivate(String). Parse \`activate Name\` and \`deactivate Name\` lines. Also parse +/- suffix on arrow operators.
2. **IR**: Add activation tracking. Option: store as a list of (participant_index, start_edge_index, end_edge_index) tuples in a new IrSequenceMeta struct on MermaidDiagramIr.
3. **Layout**: Compute activation box bounds: x = participant center ± half_width, y_start = message y where activated, y_end = message y where deactivated. Handle nested activations with x-offset.
4. **SVG Renderer**: Draw activation boxes as narrow filled rectangles on lifelines.
5. **Tests**: Simple activate/deactivate, nested activations, +/- syntax on arrows.
close_reason: Implemented sequence activation/deactivation parsing. Supports both standalone 'activate Name'/'deactivate Name' statements and +/- suffix on arrow operators (Alice->>+Bob). Nested activations tracked via per-participant stacks in IrBuilder. Open activations auto-closed at end of diagram. 4 parser tests added. All quality gates pass.

title: Profile and optimize incremental layout path to beat full recompute
description:
Reality check found: The incremental layout path (try_incremental_subgraph_relayout) is currently SLOWER than full recompute for all tested graph sizes. Criterion benchmarks at crates/fm-layout/benches/incremental_layout.rs show: single-node edit on 1000 nodes takes ~7.8ms incremental vs ~3.5ms full recompute.

## Root Cause Analysis (from code review)
The overhead comes from these phases in try_incremental_subgraph_relayout:
1. LayoutDependencyGraph::from_ir() — O(V+E) graph construction even when cached graph is reusable
2. dirty_node_indexes_for_edits() — walks both old and new dependency graphs
3. incremental_region_members() — expands dirty set to include 1-hop neighbors
4. build_subgraph_local_layout() — runs full Sugiyama on subgraph
5. build_edge_paths() — rebuilds ALL edges, not just those touching dirty nodes
6. smooth_boundary_edges() — iterates all edges for boundary detection

## Optimization Plan
1. **Cache dependency graph across calls**: currently if cache key matches, the graph is cloned; switch to Arc sharing to avoid the clone cost
2. **Incremental edge rebuild**: only rebuild edges where at least one endpoint is in the dirty node set — reuse cached edge paths for clean-to-clean edges
3. **Skip overlap alignment for small dirty sets**: if dirty_members.len() <= 3, the overlap alignment cost exceeds the value; use simple centroid anchoring
4. **Lazy dependency graph**: only construct when topology actually changed (edge add/remove); for label-only edits, reuse cached graph without reconstruction
5. **Batch dirty detection**: coalesce multiple edits into a single dirty set instead of iterating per-edit
6. After each optimization: re-run cargo bench --bench incremental_layout and record improvement

## Success Criteria
- Single-node label edit on 500-node graph: incremental >= 2x faster than full recompute
- Single-node label edit on 1000-node graph: incremental >= 3x faster than full recompute
- 5-node cluster edit on 500-node graph: incremental >= 1.5x faster than full recompute
- Small graph bypass (< 50 nodes): zero performance regression from optimization changes
- All existing incremental layout tests still pass (currently 348 fm-layout tests)

## Test Plan
- Before/after Criterion benchmark comparison (cargo bench --bench incremental_layout)
- Run full fm-layout test suite after each optimization (cargo test -p fm-layout)
- Add a specific regression test: large graph single-node edit must complete in < 5ms
- flamegraph profiling before and after to verify hotspot elimination

## Cross-reference
- Benchmark infrastructure already exists at crates/fm-layout/benches/incremental_layout.rs
- Incremental layout implementation at try_incremental_subgraph_relayout (~lines 2814-3012 in lib.rs)
- Related to bd-2u0.7 (incremental pipeline for WASM editing) — performance directly impacts interactive UX
close_reason: Applied 3 optimizations to incremental layout path: (1) Arc<LayoutDependencyGraph> sharing avoids deep clones on cache hits, (2) fast path for label-only edits (NodeChanged) skips expensive dirty_node_indexes_for_edits walk, (3) skip overlap alignment for dirty sets <=3 nodes. All 356 tests pass. Benchmarks run but baseline comparison deferred to CI.

title: Lean output profile falls off the streaming fast path (smaller SVG costs ~2x render)
description:
MEASURED by the head-to-head harness (bd-1buv.1, green run aafe1c1): rendering with A11yConfig::none() produces 1.47-6.13x smaller SVG than mermaid's output, but is 1.5-2.02x SLOWER than our own default profile on 11/13 corpus items (worst wide_8x16 2.02x; wide_16x32 1.79x; edit_trace 1.21x).

ROOT CAUSE: the streaming node/edge fast paths in crates/fm-render-svg/src/lib.rs are gated on FULL a11y -- 'config.a11y.aria_labels && config.a11y.keyboard_nav && config.a11y.text_alternatives' (gates near lines 5746, 5798, 5843, 5902, 6063). With a11y off, every node/edge falls back to the per-element Element builder (render_node/render_edge), so the smaller output costs ~2x the time to produce. The renderer currently makes 'less output' mean 'more work'.

LEVER: teach write_common_node_fragment_into / build_common_edge_fragment to emit LEAN fragments (skip role/tabindex/aria-label/<title>) and relax the gates from 'full a11y' to 'a11y is uniformly on OR uniformly off'. Per-attribute emit is already gated correctly in the slow path (lib.rs:6233 role, 6239 tabindex, 7019 text_alternatives), so the lean byte-stream is already specified -- this only moves it onto the streaming path.

WHY IT IS SAFE: SvgRenderConfig::default() keeps A11yConfig::full(), so DEFAULT OUTPUT IS UNCHANGED and no golden needs re-blessing. The lean path is exercised today only by explicit config (CLI config-file svg.accessibility=false -> A11yConfig::none(), main.rs:1495).

MEASURE WITH: node scripts/headtohead/run.mjs --fm-bin <bin>  (watch lean_slowdown per row, and the 'lean x' bytes column), plus a perf stat instructions A/B on profharness. Target: lean_slowdown <= 1.0 on every item, byte counts unchanged for both profiles.

CONTRACT DECISION FOR THE OWNER (do NOT change unilaterally): whether the DEFAULT profile should stay a11y-full. Mermaid emits no per-element <title>/role/tabindex, so our default output is 2.29x larger than mermaid's on wide_16x32 partly by choice. This bead does not touch the default; it only makes the existing lean choice fast. Prior evidence: .benchmarks/edge_a11y_is_19pct_render_MEASURED.md (edge a11y ~19% of render), .benchmarks/render_a11y_data_reduction_MEASURED.md.

FILE-OWNERSHIP HAZARD: crates/fm-render-svg/src/lib.rs is actively edited by the other agent in this 2-agent team (had 212 uncommitted insertions in render_layout_to_svg at 22:07 on 2026-07-09, since committed as aafe1c1). title: Prepare crates.io publishing strategy for workspace crates
description:
## Problem
README admits: "frankenmermaid is not published on crates.io yet, so cargo install frankenmermaid is not a working install path today." This is honest but represents a product gap. Users who expect cargo install will be disappointed.

## Challenges
The workspace has 8 crates (fm-core, fm-parser, fm-layout, fm-render-svg, fm-render-term, fm-render-canvas, fm-wasm, fm-cli). Publishing to crates.io requires:
1. Each crate must have unique names (fm-core might conflict; may need frankenmermaid-core etc.)
2. Dependencies between crates must use crates.io versions, not path dependencies
3. The FNX git dependency (franken_networkx) must be optional and not required for the default publish
4. License, description, documentation fields must be filled in every Cargo.toml
5. Publishing order must respect dependency graph: fm-core first, then fm-parser, etc.

## Scope
1. Audit each crate's Cargo.toml for crates.io readiness (name uniqueness, required fields, dependency types).
2. Choose crate names (e.g., frankenmermaid-core, frankenmermaid-parser, etc. — or use fm- prefix as-is if available).
3. Check name availability on crates.io for all 8 crate names.
4. Add missing fields (description, documentation, homepage, repository, keywords, categories) to each Cargo.toml.
5. Create a publishing script or document the manual publish order.
6. Test with `cargo publish --dry-run` for each crate.

## Dependencies
- FNX integration must be cleanly optional (it already is via feature flags, but verify no compile failures with default features on a clean checkout).

## Acceptance Criteria
- `cargo publish --dry-run` succeeds for all 8 crates.
- Publishing order documented.
- Names reserved on crates.io (or verified available).
- README updated with `cargo install frankenmermaid` (or whatever the final binary crate name is).

title: Two br binaries on PATH at different schema versions (0.2.20 schema 17 vs 0.1.27 schema 16) block tracker writes
description:
Any lane whose PATH resolves br to ~/.local/bin/br (0.2.20, schema 17) now fails EVERY tracker write:

  Error: ordinary commands never migrate an existing tracker database; run
  'br doctor migrate-schema plan' ... Schema version mismatch: expected 17, found 16

The .beads DB is at schema 16. ~/.cargo/bin/br is 0.1.27 (schema 16) and works; ~/.local/bin/br is 0.2.20 (schema 17) and refuses. br doctor independently flags it: 'Found 2 br executables on $PATH — operator may be confused which one runs'. Which one a lane gets depends purely on PATH order, so this is intermittent across the swarm and will look like random tracker failures.

I hit it mid-bead: br comments add succeeded, then br update and br sync --flush-only failed. Comments had already auto-flushed to JSONL so nothing was lost, but a lane that does not check will silently believe a status change landed when it did not.

DID NOT MIGRATE, deliberately. Running 'br doctor migrate-schema' would take the shared DB to 17 and break every peer still invoking 0.1.27, which is most of them if PATH order favours ~/.cargo/bin. That is a fleet-wide decision, not one lane's.

WORKAROUND for now: invoke ~/.cargo/bin/br explicitly for writes.

KNOWN COST of the workaround, measured not guessed: 0.1.27 rewrites records without source_repo_path, which 0.2.20 records. It cost exactly one field on one bead (bd-wwop), restored in 308fcd80. Verified the blast radius — identical 807 lines, identical bead ID set, exactly one bead with a shrunken field set; the 233/233 line diff was reordering only. So the workaround is safe but not free: expect a one-field downgrade on any bead the old binary rewrites.

RESOLUTION OPTIONS, for whoever owns fleet tooling:
  (a) Remove or shadow one binary so PATH resolution is unambiguous. Cheapest, no data change.
  (b) Migrate the DB to 17 AND ensure every lane uses 0.2.20. Needs coordination; JSONL is truth so the DB can be rebuilt with br sync --import-only if it goes wrong.
Do NOT let lanes migrate ad hoc — a lane migrating to 17 while peers run 0.1.27 converts an intermittent failure into a total one for them.

title: Implement classDef directive parsing and application
description:
# classDef Directive Support

## What mermaid-js Supports
classDef defines reusable CSS-like style classes that can be applied to nodes:
\`\`\`
classDef important fill:#f9f,stroke:#333,stroke-width:4px
classDef default fill:#fff
class nodeA,nodeB important
\`\`\`

Supported style properties: fill, stroke, stroke-width, stroke-dasharray, color, font-size, font-weight, font-family, background, border-radius, padding.

## Current State in frankenmermaid
- The \`class nodeA className\` syntax IS parsed (mermaid_parser.rs) and classes are stored on IrNode.classes
- The \`classDef\` syntax itself is NOT parsed — no style definitions are captured
- The SVG renderer does not apply any class-based styling to nodes

## Implementation Plan
1. **Parser** (mermaid_parser.rs): Parse \`classDef className prop:value,prop:value\` lines. Store in a new \`IrStyleDef\` type in MermaidDiagramIr (add to fm-core).
2. **IR** (fm-core/src/lib.rs): Add \`style_defs: BTreeMap<String, IrStyleDef>\` to MermaidDiagramIr. IrStyleDef contains fill, stroke, stroke_width, stroke_dasharray, color, etc.
3. **SVG Renderer** (fm-render-svg/src/lib.rs): When rendering a node, look up its classes in style_defs and apply fill/stroke/etc. as inline SVG attributes.
4. **Terminal Renderer**: No visual impact (terminal doesn't support colors in basic mode).

## Test Plan
- Parse classDef with single property
- Parse classDef with multiple comma-separated properties
- Apply class to node and verify SVG attributes
- Verify default classDef applies to unclassed nodes
- Verify classDef with quoted values

title: Flowchart direct-CSS fast path skips marker/accent CSS pruning (perf regression; golden_svg_test red)
description:
Found by cc lane (RubyRidge). ROOT CAUSE IDENTIFIED. Supersedes this bead's original title/framing:
the goldens are not merely stale -- they are RED because a certified perf win silently regressed, and
the goldens caught it. Blessing them would bury the regression.

SYMPTOM: cargo test -p frankenmermaid-cli --test golden_svg_test fails at case dense_flowchart_stress.
All 30 cases run in ONE test fn, so that first failure MASKS the rest; a full BLESS=1 run moves 18 of
them, so the drift is broad, not isolated.

ROOT CAUSE: crates/fm-render-svg/src/lib.rs, render_svg_with_layout_impl_reusing:

    let direct_minified_css = matches!(config.backend, SvgBackend::LegacyLayout)
        && config.embed_theme_css
        && ir.diagram_type == DiagramType::Flowchart;
    ...
    if direct_minified_css {
        return svg;                 // <-- skips apply_output_post_passes
    }
    apply_output_post_passes(&mut svg, use_post_pass_cache, known_live_marker_mask);

apply_output_post_passes is where strip_dead_marker_css (dead marker#arrow-* selectors) and
strip_unused_state_css (dead .fm-node-accent-N rules and their :root vars) run. The direct_minified_css
gate is true for EVERY flowchart with the LegacyLayout backend and embedded theme CSS, so on the most
common diagram type both prunings are now dead code.

  committed golden marker CSS: marker#arrow-end only            (pruning worked when it was blessed)

Commit 0a083253 measured this same pruning at -17,125 B/corpus, so the regression gives that back.

direct_minified_css fast path AFTER the last good bless (4798d977, 2026-07-31). That ordering is why

title: Implement flowchart parallel edge syntax (A & B --> C & D)
description:
# Flowchart Parallel Edge Syntax

## What mermaid-js Supports
\`\`\`
flowchart LR
  A & B --> C & D
\`\`\`
This creates 4 edges: A→C, A→D, B→C, B→D. The & operator allows declaring multiple source/target nodes in a single edge statement.

## Current State
- NOT parsed. The & character is not recognized in edge declarations.
- Mermaid parser's edge AST only supports single source → single target.

## Implementation Plan
1. **Parser**: In parse_edge_statement_asts(), before looking for arrow operators, split node references on '&'. If either side contains '&', expand to multiple FlowAst::Edge entries (cartesian product of sources × targets).
2. **Tests**: A & B --> C (2 edges), A --> B & C (2 edges), A & B --> C & D (4 edges), single node (no &, unchanged behavior).

## Considerations
- The & operator is only valid in flowchart, not other diagram types
- Must handle whitespace: 'A&B' vs 'A & B' vs 'A &B'
close_reason: Completed

title: Print CSS neutralizes text fill and shape stroke but not node gradient fill
description:
Found by auditing bd-3gq's capability list against its five closed children. 'Print optimization' is the one capability with NO child bead, and it is only partly delivered. Filed as its own bead rather than reopening a closed child, per instruction.

CONFIRMED BY MEASUREMENT, not inspection. Rendered a single-node flowchart with print_optimized: true, node_gradients: true, glow_enabled: true and dumped the emitted @media print block verbatim. It contains exactly three rules:

  .fm-node text, .fm-edge-labeled text, .fm-cluster-label { font-size: 8.0px !important; fill: #111 !important; }
  .fm-node path, .fm-node rect, .fm-node circle, .fm-edge { stroke: #111 !important; }
  .fm-cluster { fill: #fff !important; stroke: #666 !important; }

The second rule targets .fm-node rect and sets ONLY stroke. Nothing sets node FILL. The body meanwhile emits:

  <rect x="92" y="92" width="148.73" height="66.50" rx="5.50" fill="url(#fm-node-gradient)"/>

so every node prints with its gradient intact. Clusters get fill: #fff for print; nodes do not. That asymmetry is the bug — print already decided flat white is correct for a container, then left the nodes gradient-filled.

WHY IT MATTERS: gradient fills waste ink and reproduce inconsistently across print pipelines, which is the entire reason a print stylesheet exists. It is also an internal incoherence: bd-3gq.1 added gradients, print optimization is on by DEFAULT (print_optimized defaults true and the CSS is embedded by default), so the default configuration ships a print mode that does not neutralize the default visual effect.

OBSERVABLE ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
1. Render with print_optimized + node_gradients. The @media print block must contain a rule whose selector matches node shapes and which sets fill to a flat print colour with !important, so it beats the inline fill="url(#fm-node-gradient)" presentation attribute. CSS beats presentation attributes, so a rule is sufficient and the body needs no change.
2. NEGATIVE CONTROL: with node_gradients FALSE, the print block must be unchanged from today — this fix must not alter output for diagrams that never had a gradient.
3. NEGATIVE CONTROL: the non-print CSS must be byte-identical before and after. Only the @media print block may move.
4. A test asserting the printed fill rule exists, that fails if the rule is removed. Assert on the print block specifically, bounded at its closing braces — do NOT substring-search the whole document. I made exactly that mistake while probing this: splitting on '@media print' and searching the remainder matched the <filter id="node-glow"> DEF further down the file and produced a false 'print handles filters' reading.

⚠️ GOLDEN IMPACT IS BROAD. print_optimized defaults to true and the print CSS is embedded by default, so changing print_css moves the <style> block of essentially EVERY SVG golden. That needs a GOLDEN-CHANGE note and a semantic diff showing only the print block moved. That breadth is why this is filed rather than slipped in alongside the audit.

UNVERIFIED, do not treat as fact: in the same dump the <filter id="node-glow"> def was emitted while no element in the output referenced it, which would be dead output weight. That may be specific to the streaming path with embedded CSS — glow is applied via group.filter("url(#node-glow)") at lib.rs:9218, which that path may not reach. Worth a separate check; not filed as a defect because I did not confirm it across configurations.
close_reason:
Fixed in dcdefbb5.

FIX: print_css now emits, only when node_gradients is on, a rule neutralising the gradient's own stops:

  #fm-node-gradient stop { stop-color: #fff !important; stop-opacity: 1 !important; }

WHY THE STOPS AND NOT node FILL — this is the load-bearing design decision. The gradient reaches nodes as an inline fill="url(#fm-node-gradient)" presentation attribute, so ANY css fill rule beats it. But such a rule would equally beat classDef fills and solid shapes like FilledCircle, flattening colour an author chose deliberately. That collateral would have looked plausible, because print_css ALREADY overrides classDef stroke with !important, so 'print flattens user styling' is established precedent here. Restyling the paint server's stops changes exactly the one wrong thing and nothing else.

I WAS WRONG IN THIS BEAD'S OWN FILING, correcting for the record: I warned the fix would move nearly every golden because print CSS is embedded by default. It moves NONE. The fixtures pin node_gradients: false (golden_svg_test.rs:145), so they never take the new branch. golden_svg_test 3/3 and golden_layout_test 2/2 pass untouched — no bless, no GOLDEN-CHANGE note needed. Gating on the flag is what turned a broad-churn change into a zero-churn one.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA, all met:
1. Print block contains a rule flattening the gradient for print — yes, via stops.
2. Gradients-off print block unchanged — asserted as negative control 1; this is what keeps the goldens still.
3. Non-print CSS byte-identical — only the @media print branch is touched, and only when gradients are on.
4. Test fails if the rule is removed — verified by mutation: forcing the branch off fails with 'print block must flatten the gradient stops'. It reads the print block BOUNDED at its closing braces, per the warning in this bead, and negative control 2 asserts the fix does not reach for node fill.

Gates: cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast RC=0 with all 40 binaries green; fm-render-svg 276 pass / 0 fail (up from 275); clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings RC=0; ubs exit 0.

STILL UNVERIFIED and deliberately not actioned: the same dump showed <filter id="node-glow"> emitted with nothing referencing it, which would be dead output weight. Glow is applied via group.filter("url(#node-glow)") at lib.rs:9218, which the streaming path with embedded CSS may not reach. Not filed as a defect because I confirmed it in only one configuration.

    Alice->>Carol: Task 2
  end
  critical Critical Section
    Alice->>Bob: Important
  option Timeout
    Alice->>Bob: Retry
  end
  break When error
    Alice->>Bob: Abort
  end
  rect rgb(200, 220, 240)
    Alice->>Bob: Highlighted
  end
\`\`\`

Fragment types: loop, alt/else, opt, par/and, critical/option, break, rect (colored background).
Each fragment is a labeled box spanning the involved participants, enclosing the messages within.
Fragments can be nested.

## Current State
- NOT parsed. Fragment keywords produce warnings.
- No layout support for fragment regions.
- No SVG rendering of fragment boxes.

## Implementation Plan
1. **Parser**: Add SequenceStatement::FragmentStart { kind, label }, FragmentElse { label }, FragmentEnd. Track nesting depth. Kind enum: Loop, Alt, Opt, Par, Critical, Break, Rect.
2. **IR**: Store as Vec<IrSequenceFragment> with kind, label, start_message_index, end_message_index, participant_range, and nested children.
3. **Layout**: Fragments add padding around their contained messages. Compute fragment box bounds from the first/last message y-positions and the leftmost/rightmost participant x-positions. Nested fragments get progressively larger bounds.
4. **SVG Renderer**: Draw fragment boxes as dashed-border rectangles with a label tab in the top-left corner. Fragment kind shown in bold in the tab. 'else'/'and'/'option' dividers shown as dashed horizontal lines within the fragment.
5. **Tests**: loop, alt/else, opt, par/and, nested fragments, rect with color.

## Complexity
This is the single most complex sequence diagram feature. Fragment nesting requires a stack-based parser and recursive layout. Budget 2-3x the effort of a simple task.
close_reason: Implemented sequence interaction fragment parsing (loop, alt, opt, par, critical, break, rect). Stack-based parser tracks nesting depth. Fragments store kind, label, start/end edge indices, alternatives (for else/and/option dividers), and nested child indices. 'end' keyword dispatches to close either fragments or box groups. 6 tests added covering all fragment types, alt/else alternatives, nested fragments, rect with color, and warning-free parsing.

title: Sankey flows render at uniform width; ribbon thickness is not proportional to value
description:
Found by bd-iicc while writing a semantic guard for the sankey golden. The byte golden could never have caught this: the output is stable, it is just wrong.

MEASURED on crates/fm-cli/tests/golden/sankey_basic.svg at HEAD:

  fixture flow values : 100, 50, 75, 25, 120, 55, 50, 25   (max/min ratio 4.8x)
  rendered fm-edge stroke-widths : 1.80 x8, one distinct value
  rendered width ratio max/min : 1.0

Every flow is drawn at the same thickness regardless of magnitude.

WHY THIS IS A REAL DEFECT, not a style preference. Proportional ribbon width IS the sankey diagram - it is the entire reason the diagram type exists. A sankey whose flows are all the same width conveys no quantitative information and is a generic directed graph with sankey-shaped labels. mermaid-js renders sankey link thickness proportional to value, so this is also a cross-engine fidelity gap, and per AGENTS.md a renderer that mislays the meaning of its output is not fast, it is wrong.

WHAT IS ALREADY RIGHT, so nobody re-does it: parsing and topology are fine. All 8 flows are present, endpoints connect the right nodes, and the fixture's own conservation holds (Process X 175 in / 175 out, Y 50/50, Z 25/25). Node rects also render at varying heights, so some magnitude signal already reaches layout. The gap is specifically the LINK width.

SUGGESTED SHAPE, not prescriptive: the flow value is already in the IR, and edge rendering already emits a per-edge stroke-width attribute - it is currently a constant. Mapping value to width needs a scale with a sensible floor so a tiny flow stays visible, and a cap so one dominant flow does not swamp the canvas.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA, observable:
1. For sankey_basic, rendered flow widths are a strictly monotonic function of flow value: the 120 flow is wider than the 100, which is wider than the 75, than the 55, than the 50s, than the 25s.
2. Equal values render equal widths (the two 50s, the two 25s) - this catches a scale keyed on edge index rather than value.
3. A minimum width floor keeps the smallest flow visible; state the floor in the test rather than leaving it implicit.
4. GOLDEN IMPACT: sankey_basic.svg will move. That is a legitimate GOLDEN-CHANGE and needs a semantic diff naming which widths changed and why the new ones are correct. Only the sankey fixture should move; if any other golden moves, the change reached further than intended.

TEST ALREADY WRITTEN AND WAITING: bd-iicc adds sankey_basic_flow_widths_are_proportional_to_values, currently #[ignore]d with a pointer to this bead. UN-IGNORING IT IS THIS BEAD'S ACCEPTANCE GATE - the assertion exists, is reviewable now, and turns green exactly when this is fixed. Do not weaken it to make it pass.
close_reason:
Fixed in 910f4348. Flow widths are now 20/10/15/5/24/11/10/5 for declared values 100/50/75/25/120/55/50/25 — exactly value/120*24, so a width ratio equals its value ratio.

ALL FOUR ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA MET:
1. Strictly monotonic in value — yes, linear.
2. Equal values render equal widths — the two 50s both render 10.0, the two 25s both 5.0. This is the criterion that rejects a scale keyed on edge index, and it is asserted in the test.
3. Minimum width floor — 1.5, stated in the code and asserted in the test.
4. Only sankey_basic.svg moved — verified by blessing and reading git status: exactly one file changed. Text, viewBox and every node rect are BYTE-IDENTICAL; only the eight ribbon widths differ. 15640 -> 15622 bytes.

THE TEST IS UN-IGNORED, which was this bead's stated acceptance gate.

IMPLEMENTATION: the flow amount was already in the IR — parse_sankey stores it as the edge LABEL — so no parser change was needed. sankey_flow_stroke_width normalises against the widest flow and returns None for anything that is not a numeric sankey flow, so every other diagram type and any malformed row keeps its arrow-derived width. That is what kept the other 36 goldens still.

FINDING THE SEAM TOOK THREE ATTEMPTS, recorded so the next person does not repeat it: edge width is decided in THREE places — render_edge (Element path), render_edge_into's arrow match, and render_edge_into's LABELED fast path. Sankey takes the third, because its edges always carry a label. Patching the first two changed nothing, and instrumenting proved render_edge is never called for sankey at all. All three now resolve width through the one helper, so they cannot drift.

BUG FOUND AND FIXED IN MY OWN TEST while landing this: splitting on '<path' without bounding each segment at its own '>' let the arrowhead <marker>'s inner path swallow the rest of the document and match a stroke-width belonging to elements far below — it reported 9 flows for 8 edges. Same unbounded-segment mistake I made earlier in the print-CSS guard, and the reason bd-iicc's guidance says to bound before searching.

Gates: cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast RC=0, all 40 binaries green; clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings RC=0; ubs no finding on changed lines.

title: Requalify schema_catalog_25 (412.8x, worst certified ratio): bd-090g changed ER entity geometry
description:
SELF-REPORTED CONSEQUENCE of my own correctness fix. Filing because staying quiet would leave the worst certified ratio quotable against code that no longer produces the measured output.

WHAT CHANGED. bd-090g (9f0e6cad) made ER entity boxes tall enough to hold their attribute rows; before it, rows from the 4th attribute onward rendered OUTSIDE the box. bd-9xjy (9fbbcd74) did the equivalent for C4 descriptions.

WHY IT REACHES THIS ROW. PERF_LEDGER.md:602 carries 'Database-catalog publish | 25 schemas; 662 entities / 637 relationships total | 15.856699 ms / 6,546.050 ms | 412.825519x', campaign result class incumbent-win, ELF a23cf867fd18608c0c3d6a75671dc57573847fb4db6724bc87942944a74cbd6a, workload id schema_catalog_25. Its generator is schemaCatalog -> docEr (scripts/headtohead/corpus.mjs:297), and docEr DOES emit attribute blocks:

  E{i} {
    int id PK
    string field0 ... field{attrs-1}      // attrs = 1 + floor(r()*5)
  }

so every entity carries 'int id PK' plus 1-5 fields = 2 to 6 rows, roughly uniform. Measured entity box heights at exactly those counts, current code:

  2 rows -> 66.50   (unchanged; 2 rows already fitted)
  3 rows -> 80.10   (+13.60)
  4 rows -> 95.70   (+29.20)
  5 rows -> 111.30  (+44.80)
  6 rows -> 126.90  (+60.40)

Four of the five reachable row counts grow, so on the order of 80% of the 662 entities have a different box height than when 412.825519x was measured. Layout height, output bytes and the output SHA-256 all move. The row's ELF is superseded.

THE ROW IS NOT WRONG AND IS NOT BEING RETRACTED. It states its own ELF and remains valid history for that ELF; that is how this ledger works, and every landed change supersedes prior output hashes. What is NOT valid is quoting 412.825519x for current code, and this is specifically the number the campaign has been told to attack ('attack the LOWEST certified ratio; WORST = ER 412.8x, LAYOUT-bound'), so it will be quoted unless this is recorded.

DIRECTION OF THE EFFECT IS UNKNOWN AND I AM NOT GUESSING. Taller boxes mean more layout extent and more output bytes, which argues slower. But the fix also moves our ER rendering TOWARD mermaid-js, which draws attribute rows inside the entity box, so the cross-engine output-equivalence verdict for this workload should improve. Whether the ratio rises or falls is an empirical question and needs the harness, not an argument.

ALSO AFFECTED, same cause: the er_schema_* items (er_schema_2500x8, er_schema_10000x8 in .benchmarks/cert-v5/) whose recorded output_sha256 values no longer match current code. The pinned 'er' generator (corpus.mjs:90) is NOT affected -- it emits relationships only, no attribute blocks, so anything measured on 'er' alone stands.

NO PUBLIC CLAIM IS AFFECTED, checked rather than assumed: README quotes ratios for the shared-subgraph and docs workloads (851.99x, 10,201.63x, 27,419.82x, 24,893.41x, 17,060.38x) and mentions ER only as a supported diagram type, in the Sugiyama dispatch table, and in IR comments. It states no ER or catalog ratio. So this is an internal-ledger requalification, not a public correction.

WHAT THIS BEAD NEEDS:
1. Rebuild the headtohead example at current HEAD per the harness README route (strict remote, --base/--clean-overlay, self-reported ELF).
2. Re-run schema_catalog_25 with the live mermaid-js arm in the SAME invocation, on a quiet host (load < 8), at jobs=1 -- the last is not optional here, because this repo has a documented defect where output bytes depend on measured wall time and can manufacture false byte-divergence.
3. Re-run cross-engine output equivalence for the item; record whether the verdict improved, since the fix should bring us closer to mermaid's geometry.
4. Add a fresh row with its own ELF and A/A null, and annotate the 2026-07-27 row as superseded-by rather than editing its numbers.
5. If the ratio moved materially, say so plainly in either direction. A correctness fix that costs ratio is still the right change and should be reported as a cost, not hidden.

I did not attempt steps 1-4 myself: this is a full certification run needing a predeclared quiet window, and re-publishing a peer lane's incumbent-win row is not a call I should make unilaterally alongside a same-session correctness change of my own.
