title: Implement superior cycle handling in Sugiyama layout
description:
This is THE core differentiator mentioned in the X thread. Mermaid-js handles cycles poorly. Our approach:

1. DETECTION: Tarjan's SCC algorithm to find all strongly connected components. Report cycle count, participants, and nesting depth.

2. MULTI-STRATEGY CYCLE BREAKING (user-configurable):
   a. GREEDY (current): Source/sink peeling. Fast, good for mostly-DAG graphs.
   b. DFS-BACK: Depth-first search, reverse back edges. Minimizes reversed edges.
   c. MINIMUM-FEEDBACK-ARC-SET: Approximation algorithm (NP-hard exact). Finds near-minimal set of edges to reverse. Better aesthetics for heavily cyclic graphs.
   d. CYCLE-AWARE: Don't break cycles at all -- render them as visible cycles with curved back-edges. This is the 'honest' approach that shows the user their cycles rather than hiding them.

3. BACK-EDGE RENDERING: For reversed edges in GREEDY/DFS/MFAS modes, provide metadata so renderers can draw them distinctly (dashed line, different color, reversed arrowhead) to communicate that these represent cycles.

4. CYCLE CLUSTER COLLAPSE: Option to collapse an entire SCC into a single 'cycle cluster' node that can be expanded. Reduces visual complexity for highly cyclic subgraphs.

5. QUALITY METRICS: Track number of reversed edges, total edge length increase from reversal, visual symmetry of cycle representation. Expose in LayoutStats.

Determinism: All strategies must be deterministic given identical input. Use stable sorting, break ties by node ID.

## Acceptance Criteria

- All functionality explicitly described above is implemented fully; no scope reduction, no feature deletions, and no silent behavioral regressions.
- Code is modular, documented where needed, and integrated with existing crates/interfaces without compatibility shims or duplicated logic.

- Diagnostics are actionable: failures/warnings include precise context and suggested remediation.
- Determinism and stability expectations are verified for affected outputs (layout/render/serialization as applicable).
- Quality gates pass: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo check --all-targets`, and relevant `cargo test` scope.

title: Implement force-directed layout algorithm
description:
Implement a deterministic force-directed (spring-electric) layout for diagrams that don't have a natural hierarchy. Used for: ER diagrams (entities with many-to-many relationships), architecture diagrams, generic graphs with no clear flow direction.

Algorithm: Fruchterman-Reingold variant with:
1. Repulsive forces: All node pairs push apart (inverse-square law). Use Barnes-Hut approximation O(n log n) for graphs > 100 nodes.
2. Attractive forces: Connected nodes pull together (Hooke's law / log-spring).
3. Cooling schedule: Start with high temperature, reduce per iteration. Use deterministic schedule (no RNG -- use hash-based initial positions).
4. Convergence: Stop when max displacement < threshold or iteration budget exhausted.
5. Overlap removal: Post-processing pass to ensure no node overlap.
6. Cluster awareness: Nodes in same IrCluster get extra attractive force.

Key: Deterministic initial placement using hash of node IDs (not random). Same input always produces same output. Iteration count configurable via LayoutConfig.

Output: Same DiagramLayout type as Sugiyama. Callers don't need to know which algorithm was used.

## Acceptance Criteria

- All functionality explicitly described above is implemented fully; no scope reduction, no feature deletions, and no silent behavioral regressions.
- Code is modular, documented where needed, and integrated with existing crates/interfaces without compatibility shims or duplicated logic.

title: Implement tree and radial layout algorithms
description:
Implement Reingold-Tilford tree layout and radial variant for hierarchical diagrams. Used for: mindmaps, org charts, file trees, decision trees.

1. Post-order traversal to compute subtree widths

Radial layout variant:

title: Implement specialized layouts for timeline, gantt, sankey, kanban, grid
description:
Implement purpose-built layout algorithms for diagram types that don't fit general graph layout:

1. TIMELINE LAYOUT: Linear horizontal arrangement. Time periods evenly spaced. Events stacked vertically under each period. Sections as labeled bands. Simple arithmetic positioning.

2. GANTT LAYOUT: Horizontal bar chart on time axis. Tasks as bars with start/end. Dependencies as arrows between bars. Critical path highlighting. Sections as swim lanes. Calendar grid background.

3. SANKEY LAYOUT: Flow-conserving layout. Nodes in columns, edges as variable-width bands. Uses iterative relaxation to minimize edge crossings while maintaining flow conservation (inspired by d3-sankey algorithm). Node heights proportional to flow.

4. KANBAN LAYOUT: Fixed columns (swim lanes). Cards stacked vertically in columns. WIP limit indicators. Simple grid-based positioning.

5. GRID/BLOCK LAYOUT: CSS-grid-like positioning with column/row spans. Used for block diagrams. Cells sized by content, spans merged.

6. PIE/RADAR LAYOUT: Polar coordinate systems. Pie: sectors by proportion. Radar: axes from center, data points on axes connected by polygons.

Each layout produces DiagramLayout with same interface as Sugiyama/force-directed. Specialized metadata (e.g. time axis ticks for gantt) stored in layout extensions.

title: Improve crossing minimization with advanced heuristics
description:
Upgrade the barycenter crossing minimization in the Sugiyama pipeline with more sophisticated heuristics for better edge routing aesthetics:

1. SIFTING: After barycenter, apply sifting heuristic -- try moving each node to every position in its layer, keep the position with fewest crossings. O(n^2) per layer but significant quality improvement.

2. TRANSPOSE: Pairwise swapping of adjacent nodes if it reduces crossings. Iterate until no improvement.

3. GLOBAL SIFTING: Move nodes across layers (re-rank) if it reduces total crossings. Bounded to prevent infinite loops.

4. EDGE BUNDLING: Group edges with similar source/target layers and route them through shared waypoints. Reduces visual clutter for dense graphs.

5. LONG EDGE OPTIMIZATION: For edges spanning multiple ranks, ensure dummy nodes are well-positioned to minimize bends. Current implementation uses median; try also left-right centering.

6. PORT ORDERING: When a node has multiple ports, order them to minimize crossings of attached edges. Currently ports are arbitrary; this matters for class/ER diagrams.

Quality metric: track crossing count before/after each heuristic. Expose in LayoutStats so users can see improvement.

title: Implement orthogonal edge routing with channel assignment
description:
Implement proper orthogonal (Manhattan-style) edge routing that produces clean, non-overlapping edge paths:

1. CHANNEL ASSIGNMENT: Between each pair of adjacent ranks, assign horizontal routing channels. Edges that need to turn are assigned to channels to avoid overlap.

2. NUDGE ALGORITHM: After initial routing, nudge edge segments to reduce total edge length and improve spacing.

3. CONFLICT RESOLUTION: When edges must cross, minimize crossing angle and ensure crossing point is visually clear (not on a bend).

4. POLYLINE SIMPLIFICATION: Remove unnecessary waypoints from edge paths. If three consecutive waypoints are collinear, remove the middle one.

5. SPLINE OPTION: As alternative to orthogonal, offer cubic Bezier spline routing. Control points computed from waypoint geometry for smooth curves. Configurable per-edge or globally.

6. SELF-LOOP ROUTING: Special handling for edges where source == target. Route as a loop going out the right/bottom and returning to left/top.

7. PARALLEL EDGE ROUTING: When multiple edges connect the same pair of nodes, offset them to be visually distinguishable.

This significantly improves visual quality over the current waypoint-based routing.

title: Topological Persistence for Stable Layout Features
description:
## Topological Persistence for Stable Layout Features

Apply persistent homology (topological data analysis) to identify and preserve stable topological features of diagram layouts across edits, preventing "layout earthquakes" where small edits cause large visual changes.

## Mathematical Foundation
Persistent homology tracks the birth and death of topological features (connected components, loops, voids) as a filtration parameter varies. For diagram layouts:

**Construction:**
1. Build a filtration on the node positions: start with all nodes as isolated points (ε=0), increase ε, connect nodes when distance < ε.
2. At each ε, compute the Betti numbers: β_0 = connected components, β_1 = loops.
3. Track when features appear (birth) and disappear (death) as ε increases.
4. Features with long persistence (death - birth >> 0) are STABLE topological features of the layout.

**Application to layout stability:**
- Stable features (high persistence) should be preserved across edits. If a single-node edit causes a high-persistence feature to vanish, the layout change was disproportionate — trigger stabilization.
- Stabilization: constrain the new layout to preserve all features with persistence > threshold. This prevents "layout earthquakes" while allowing local adjustments.

**Persistence diagram:** Plot (birth, death) for each feature. Points far from the diagonal are stable features; points near the diagonal are noise. The bottleneck distance between two persistence diagrams measures how much the layout's topological structure changed.

**Wasserstein distance (stability metric):**
W_p(D_1, D_2) = inf_γ (Σ ||x - γ(x)||^p)^{1/p}
where γ ranges over bijections between persistence diagrams D_1, D_2.
If W_∞(D_before, D_after) > threshold → layout change is too disruptive → stabilize.

## Key Papers
- Edelsbrunner, Letscher & Zomorodian, "Topological Persistence and Simplification" (DCG 2002)
- Carlsson, "Topology and Data" (AMS 2009) — survey
- Cohen-Steiner, Edelsbrunner & Harer, "Stability of Persistence Diagrams" (DCG 2007) — stability theorem
- Ghrist, "Barcodes: The Persistent Topology of Data" (AMS 2008) — accessible introduction

## Implementation in FrankenMermaid
1. Implement Vietoris-Rips filtration on node positions (or alpha complex for efficiency).
2. Compute persistent homology using a matrix reduction algorithm (standard persistence algorithm).
3. Or use the `gudhi` or `ripser` crate binding (if available for Rust), or implement from scratch for educational value.
4. After each edit: compute persistence diagram of new layout, compare with pre-edit diagram.
5. If Wasserstein distance > threshold: add constraints to preserve high-persistence features, re-run layout.
6. Expose persistence visualization in demo: show barcode diagram alongside layout.
7. Decision contract: adopt if layout stability measurably improved (fewer "earthquake" events) AND computation overhead < 50ms per edit.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Persistent homology computed for 2D node positions (β_0 and β_1)
- [ ] Persistence diagram correctly identifies stable clusters and loops in layout
- [ ] Wasserstein distance computed between pre/post edit persistence diagrams
- [ ] Layout stabilization constraint prevents high-persistence feature destruction
- [ ] Computation time < 50ms for 1000-node diagrams
- [ ] Demo visualization: persistence barcode displayed alongside diagram
- [ ] Decision contract: specific adoption threshold for stability improvement

All quality gates pass (check, clippy, fmt, 236/236 tests).

title: Unreferenced fm-node-gradient def on all four dedicated chart renderers
description:
SECOND INSTANCE of the dead-<defs> class bd-a6uk closed, found by the generic invariant test that bead added rather than by inspection. That is the point of the invariant: it generalises.

MEASURED at default config, one fm-cli render per type, counting <defs> ids that never reappear as url(#id):

  flowchart LR       ids=2  dead: -
  sequenceDiagram    ids=2  dead: -
  classDiagram       ids=2  dead: -
  stateDiagram-v2    ids=2  dead: -
  erDiagram          ids=2  dead: -
  journey            ids=1  dead: -
  mindmap            ids=1  dead: -
  gitGraph           ids=1  dead: -
  timeline           ids=1  dead: -
  gantt              ids=1  dead: fm-node-gradient
  pie                ids=1  dead: fm-node-gradient
  quadrantChart      ids=1  dead: fm-node-gradient
  xychart-beta       ids=1  dead: fm-node-gradient

Four of thirteen types, and it is 283 bytes each — bigger than bd-a6uk's 166:

  gantt         5278 bytes total, 283 in the def = 5.4%, url refs 0
  pie           6438 bytes total, 283 = 4.4%, url refs 0
  quadrantChart 6761 bytes total, 283 = 4.2%, url refs 0
  xychart-beta  8070 bytes total, 283 = 4.2%, url refs 0

MECHANISM, and it is structural rather than incidental. node_gradient_svg returns Some purely on config.node_gradients (default ON) and the def is streamed into the gradients slot at lib.rs:3719. But these four types are each handled by a DEDICATED renderer that returns early, at lib.rs:3798 xychart, 3817 pie, 3825 quadrant, 3832 gantt, and none of them reaches the generic node path where every fill="url(#fm-node-gradient)" is written. So the def is emitted for a consumer that is unreachable by construction on these types, not merely absent from this fixture.

FIX SHAPE. Gate the gradient def on the same condition the dispatch uses: suppress it when the render will take one of the four dedicated chart paths. The predicate is computable at defs time because it reads only ir (xy_chart_meta / pie_meta with non-empty slices / quadrant_meta / Gantt+gantt_meta).

THE GATES MUST BE IN LOCKSTEP, and this is the whole risk. There are FIVE conditions to keep in agreement — four dispatch branches plus the new defs gate — which is exactly the shape that produced the fast-path-drops-a-feature family (bd-678053a) and this bead's own predecessor. Extract ONE predicate used by both sides rather than restating the conditions.

THE DANGEROUS DIRECTION IS THE OPPOSITE ONE, and bd-a6uk's invariant does NOT yet catch it: if one of these renderers later starts referencing the gradient, suppressing the def yields url(#fm-node-gradient) pointing at nothing — invalid SVG, unpainted shapes. The existing test only asserts declared-but-unreferenced. It must be made BIDIRECTIONAL (also: no url(#id) may reference an id absent from <defs>) and run across diagram types, or this fix installs a silent failure mode.

Cross-checked so the next lane does not redo it: no undeclared url(#...) reference exists on any of the four types today, so the bidirectional assertion is satisfiable as written.

ALTERNATIVE CONSIDERED AND REJECTED FOR NOW: extend the existing strip_unused_markers output post-pass, which already collects every url(#id) in the finished document and would be exact by construction. Rejected because it early-returns Some(0) when the document has no <marker (true for exactly these chart types), and because its return value feeds the memoized CSS post-pass feature key — restructuring it risks cache correctness another lane built (212a285, e91eb82) for 283 bytes. Revisit if a third instance of this class appears, at which point the post-pass becomes the cheaper total fix.

EXPECTED GOLDEN IMPACT: gantt_basic, pie_basic and quadrant_basic are golden cases, but golden_svg_test pins node_gradients: false, so they never emit the def. Verify rather than assume.
close_reason:
Fixed by 569261ef.

FIX: two gates, one truth. takes_dedicated_chart_renderer is now the single source for the xychart/pie/quadrant/gantt dispatch condition, and gradient_def_emitted is the single answer to 'is the def actually in this document', read by BOTH the <defs> slot and print_css. The bead asked for one predicate rather than five restatements; that is what landed.

MEASURED, default config, one fm-cli render per type, before -> after:
  gantt         5278 -> 4910  (-368, 7.0%)
  pie           6438 -> 6076  (-362, 5.6%)
  quadrantChart 6761 -> 6399  (-362, 5.4%)
  xychart-beta  8070 -> 7708  (-362, 4.5%)
  flowchart (3 nodes)  8513 -> 8513, verified BYTE-IDENTICAL programmatically
Per type: 283 bytes of <linearGradient> def plus 79 bytes of print CSS.

SCOPE GREW BY ONE ITEM DURING THE FIX, and it was the right call rather than a separate bead: gating the def alone left bd-ccni's '#fm-node-gradient stop { ... }' print rule selecting an id no longer in the document -- 79 more dead bytes, and a cleaner-cut dead selector than before. print_css's parameter is renamed node_gradients -> gradient_def_emitted because that rename IS the fix: on these four types the two predicates differ, which is precisely what nobody had noticed.

THE BEAD'S CENTRAL WARNING WAS HONOURED. It said the dangerous direction is a url(#...) with no def, and that bd-a6uk's invariant did not yet catch it. It does now: defs_and_url_references_agree_across_diagram_types is BIDIRECTIONAL and swept across 13 parsed diagram types, and also asserts no CSS rule styles an absent def id. Cases are built by PARSING real Mermaid rather than hand-assembling metadata, because a hand-built IR can miss the condition a dispatch branch actually tests (pie slices / xy series non-empty) -- which is the gate under test.

NEGATIVE CONTROLS, all three directions measured:
  gate reverted to unconditional -> 'gantt: defs declared but never referenced: [fm-node-gradient]' plus 'gantt: gradient def and its referrer must appear together'
  gate INVERTED, suppressing the def where it IS used -> 'flowchart: url(#...) references with no matching def: [fm-node-gradient, fm-node-gradient]'
So the dangerous direction is genuinely detected, not merely asserted. File restored byte-identically (diff -q) after each control.

LOCKSTEP GUARD for the drift risk the bead flagged: the four dispatch branches keep their own meta bindings and cannot literally call the predicate, so dedicated_chart_predicate_matches_gradient_referrer_presence pins it to observed behaviour instead -- true exactly when no url(#fm-node-gradient) referrer is emitted, and the def present iff its referrer is. Changing a dispatch condition without the predicate fails the test.

DEFERRED, named rather than quietly dropped: render_scene_document_with_ir also emits the print block, and the only gradient-def emission anywhere is the site gated here, so that print rule may be dead on the scene path too. NOT fixed: I have not established what the scene path emits, and guessing there is exactly how the opposite (dangling-reference) defect gets introduced. Worth a follow-up bead if anyone touches that path.

ALTERNATIVE REJECTED as the bead anticipated: extending strip_unused_markers would be exact by construction but early-returns when the document has no <marker -- true for exactly these four types -- and its return value feeds the memoized CSS post-pass key, so restructuring risks cache correctness another lane built (212a285, e91eb82) for 362 bytes. Revisit at instance three, at which point the post-pass becomes the cheaper total fix.

BEAD PREDICTION CONFIRMED: no golden moved. golden_svg_test pins node_gradients: false, so gantt_basic/pie_basic/quadrant_basic never emitted the def. No bless, no GOLDEN-CHANGE note.

NO LEDGER ROW: output-correctness fix, no timing asserted anywhere.

GATES: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings clean (rch remote); cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast 40/40 suites green, 0 failures; fm-render-svg 279 pass / 0 fail; ubs exit 0 with no finding in the new code; cargo fmt --check clean on every hunk this commit authored. Pushed to main and master at 569261ef.

title: strip_unused_state_css: ~20 full-document scans, single-pass them (byte-identical; helps DEFAULT profile too)
description:
PROFILE-DRIVEN. Symbolized perf record on wide_8x16 (bc56f72) showed frames present ONLY under the lean profile: <&str as Pattern>::is_contained_in 6.96%, StrSearcher 4.93%, String::replace_range 1.41%, __memmove_avx_unaligned_erms 7.00% (vs 2.85% default).

ROOT CAUSE: strip_unused_state_css (crates/fm-render-svg/src/lib.rs:355) early-returns on 'svg.len() > POST_PASS_MAX_SVG_BYTES' (= 100_000, lib.rs:298). If it does NOT return, it full-scans the document ~20 times:
  * 5x STATE_CLASSES .contains() over the body
  * 8x 'fm-node-accent-N' .contains() over the body (std::array::from_fn at lib.rs:406 -- note the comment above it claims a single scan, but the code is 8 separate contains())
  * 8x 'var(--fm-accent-N)' .contains() over the WHOLE svg (lib.rs:434)
str::contains on an ABSENT needle scans the entire document. Absent is the common case, so this is worst-case O(n*k) with k~20.

THE GATE IS PROFILE-DEPENDENT: it measures OUTPUT BYTES, and the lean profile shrinks output ~31%. So mid-size diagrams fall INTO the pass only under lean:
  wide_8x16:      default 134,629 B (skips) / lean 93,077 B (RUNS)  -> lean/default 1.330x
  cyclic_scc_100: default 107,649 B (skips) / lean 73,916 B (RUNS)  -> lean/default 1.092x
MECHANISM PROVEN with a diagnostic build (cap set to 0, pass disabled for both profiles, same instr A/B protocol):
  wide_8x16 1.330x -> 0.945x ; cyclic_scc_100 1.092x -> 0.978x ; wide_12x24 (control, both skip) 0.937x -> 0.937x unchanged.

LEVER: make the presence detection SINGLE-PASS. All ~20 needles share two prefixes -- 'fm-node-' (covers fm-node-inactive / block-beta / highlighted / border-dashed / border-double / accent-1..8) and 'var(--fm-accent-'. Build one memchr::memmem::Finder for each and collect every hit in ONE traversal, reading the discriminating suffix at each match. Byte-identical: used[n] must be true iff the exact substring occurs, same as today.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND LEAN: the pass runs for EVERY diagram under 100 KB in BOTH profiles. Default-profile items that pay it today: flowchart_small_10 (13 KB), flowchart_medium_100 (72 KB), sequence_20 (43 KB), class_50 (46 KB), state_40 (35 KB), er_40 (52 KB), and every revision of edit_trace_60x20 (the live-preview workload). This is a DEFAULT-path win, not just a lean one.

DO NOT 'fix' this by gating on a profile-invariant proxy (node+edge count) instead: that changes WHICH diagrams get their CSS stripped => output bytes change => 37 goldens re-blessed + a contract decision. The single-scan fix is the byte-identical one. Keep the 100 KB cap; just make the pass cheap.

ALSO: the replace_range calls (lib.rs:381/414/440) each memmove the document tail. Once the scans are single-pass, consider collecting all strip ranges first and doing ONE rebuild (the pattern strip_unused_markers already uses: 'Single O(n) rebuild (no per-marker rescans)').

VERIFY: 26-SHA-256 corpus oracle (headtohead <corpus.json> <dump-dir>, both profiles, pristine-HEAD vs candidate) + cargo test -p fm-render-svg --lib + golden_svg. MEASURE with FM_H2H_FORCE_PROFILE + perf stat -e instructions:u two-point delta; watch flowchart_medium_100 / sequence_20 / class_50 / state_40 / er_40 on the DEFAULT profile, and wide_8x16 / cyclic_scc_100 on lean.

GENERALIZABLE TRAP worth grepping for: an optimization gated on OUTPUT SIZE is gated on a quantity the OUTPUT PROFILE controls.

FILE-OWNERSHIP: crates/fm-render-svg/src/lib.rs, the render post-pass region (lines ~294-450). The cod pane owns fm-layout.
close_reason: Landed: 21 full-document scans -> 2 single memmem passes (scan_body_fm_node_classes + scan_accent_var_refs). Byte-identical. CIs non-overlapping; relative CI half-width ORIG <=2.31%, lever <=1.27% (<5% bar). title: Fix npm package: publish @frankenmermaid/core to npm or correct README
description:
## Problem
The README prominently tells users:
```bash
npm install @frankenmermaid/core
```
However, this package is NOT published on npm. Verified 2026-04-09: `https://registry.npmjs.org/@frankenmermaid/core` returns HTTP 404.

The WASM build IS working: `pkg/` contains `frankenmermaid_bg.wasm` (1.0MB), `frankenmermaid.js` (53KB), `frankenmermaid.d.ts` (3.1KB), and a valid `package.json` declaring `@frankenmermaid/core` v0.1.0. The build pipeline (build-wasm.sh) works. Only the npm publish step is missing.

## Options (choose one)
**Option A (preferred): Publish to npm**
1. Ensure `pkg/package.json` metadata is complete (author, keywords, repository all look good already).
2. Run `wasm-pack publish` or `cd pkg && npm publish --access public` (scoped package needs --access public).
3. Verify post-publish: `npm info @frankenmermaid/core`.
4. Set up CI to auto-publish on release tags (add to `.github/workflows/ci.yml`).

**Option B: Correct README until ready to publish**
1. Replace `npm install @frankenmermaid/core` with honest instructions: "Build from source: `./build-wasm.sh && cp -r pkg/ your-project/`"
2. Add a "Coming soon to npm" note.

## Why This Matters
This is the #1 credibility gap found in the reality check. A user who follows the README's install instructions on the FIRST LINE will get an error. First impressions matter enormously for open source adoption.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `npm info @frankenmermaid/core` returns valid metadata, OR README install instructions are corrected to match reality.
- If published: CI workflow includes npm publish step on tagged releases.
- If corrected: README clearly states the package is not yet on npm and provides working alternative.

description:
docs/PERF_LEDGER.md KEEP rows require:

and AGENTS.md is explicit that 'computing a hash beside the run is not sufficient. The executing process must identify its own ELF.' The fm-layout criterion benches do not self-report, so a measured fm-layout result currently CANNOT be ledgered as a KEEP row without violating that rule.

Note this is provenance-STRENGTHENING infrastructure, not a gate change: it makes a currently-unmeetable requirement meetable, and must not be accompanied by any relaxation of the KEEP-row contract.

title: Implement subgraph direction override
description:
# Subgraph Direction Override

## What mermaid-js Supports
\`\`\`
flowchart LR
  subgraph sub1
    direction TB
    A --> B
  end
  sub1 --> C
\`\`\`
Each subgraph can have its own direction that overrides the parent graph direction. This affects layout within that subgraph only.

## Current State
- The \`direction\` keyword IS parsed within subgraphs
- The direction is stored on IrSubgraph
- The layout engine does NOT honor per-subgraph direction — it uses a single global direction

## Implementation Plan
1. **Layout** (fm-layout/src/lib.rs): In the Sugiyama layout, when processing nodes within a subgraph/cluster, check if the cluster has a direction override. If so, apply rank assignment and coordinate assignment with that direction for nodes within the cluster.
2. **Tests**: Create a flowchart with mixed directions (parent LR, child TB). Verify child nodes are laid out vertically within the horizontal parent flow.

## Complexity
This is a non-trivial layout change. The current Sugiyama implementation uses a single global direction. Supporting per-subgraph direction requires partitioning the layout into independent sub-layouts and stitching them together. Consider a phased approach: first support the feature in the IR, then implement the layout logic.
close_reason: Completed

title: REJECT: attr_static for span-metadata data-* attrs (zero-gain, reverted)
description: Reverted (working tree back to 10b1654). title: Implement class member visibility modifiers and type annotations
description:
# Class Member Visibility and Type Annotations

## What mermaid-js Supports
\`\`\`
classDiagram
  class Animal {
    +String name
    -int age
    #List~Food~ diet
    ~void breathe()
    +eat(Food food) bool
    +sleep()* : void
  }
\`\`\`
- \`+\` public, \`-\` private, \`#\` protected, \`~\` package
- Type before name for attributes, after parentheses for return types
- \`*\` suffix for abstract methods
- \`$\` suffix for static methods

## Current State
- Class blocks ARE parsed, member lines are captured
- Visibility modifiers are NOT extracted — stored as raw text in member string
- Type annotations are NOT parsed separately from names
- No rendering of visibility symbols

## Implementation Plan
1. **Parser**: When parsing class block members, extract leading +/-/#/~ as visibility. Parse \`type name\` for attributes, \`name(params) returnType\` for methods. Detect */$ suffixes.
2. **IR**: Add IrClassMember { visibility: Visibility, name: String, return_type: Option<String>, parameters: Vec<String>, is_abstract: bool, is_static: bool }.
3. **SVG Renderer**: Render three-compartment class boxes: header (class name + stereotype), attributes section, methods section. Prepend visibility symbol. Show types.
4. **Tests**: All visibility markers, attribute types, method signatures, abstract/static.
close_reason: Implemented class member visibility + three-compartment rendering. Parser already extracts +/-/#/~ visibility, types, static/abstract. Terminal renderer shows UML class boxes with compartment separators. SVG renderer shows three-compartment boxes with stereotypes, visibility symbols, type annotations, and separator lines.

title: Implement style and linkStyle directive parsing and rendering
description:
# style / linkStyle Directive Support

## What mermaid-js Supports
Inline styling for specific nodes and edges:
\`\`\`
style nodeId fill:#f9f,stroke:#333,stroke-width:4px
linkStyle 0 stroke:#ff3,stroke-width:4px,color:red
linkStyle default stroke:#333
\`\`\`

style applies to a node by ID. linkStyle applies to an edge by index (0-based declaration order) or 'default' for all edges.

## Current State
- Parser recognizes style/linkStyle lines but does not capture the property map
- No rendering path for inline styles

## Implementation Plan
1. **Parser**: Parse \`style nodeId prop:value,...\` and store as IrNodeStyle on the IrNode. Parse \`linkStyle index prop:value,...\` and store as IrEdgeStyle on the IrEdge.
2. **IR**: Add \`inline_style: Option<IrInlineStyle>\` to IrNode and IrEdge. IrInlineStyle is a BTreeMap<String, String>.
3. **SVG Renderer**: Apply inline_style as SVG attributes (fill → rect fill, stroke → rect stroke, etc.). For edges, apply to <path> elements.
4. **Tests**: Verify style is applied in SVG output, verify linkStyle by index, verify default linkStyle.

## Considerations
- Property names must be mapped from CSS-like (stroke-width) to SVG attributes
- Sanitize values to prevent XSS in SVG output
close_reason: style and linkStyle directive parsing was already implemented in extract_style_directives. SVG renderer already applies styles via resolve_node_inline_style/resolve_edge_inline_style. Now also populates structured IrInlineStyle on nodes/edges via populate_structured_styles(). Enhanced style directive to support comma-separated node IDs per mermaid-js spec. Tests pass.

title: Implement gantt date parsing, task types, and duration computation
description:
# Gantt Date/Duration/Task Type Parsing

## What mermaid-js Supports
\`\`\`
gantt
  dateFormat YYYY-MM-DD
  title Project Plan
  excludes weekends
  section Phase 1
  Design           :done, des1, 2024-01-01, 30d
  Implementation   :active, impl1, after des1, 60d
  Testing          :crit, test1, after impl1, 2024-05-01
  Milestone        :milestone, m1, after test1, 0d
\`\`\`
- dateFormat: YYYY-MM-DD, DD/MM/YYYY, etc.
- Task types: done, active, crit (critical), milestone
- Duration: Nd (days), after taskId (dependency), absolute dates
- excludes: weekends, specific dates

## Current State
- Parser recognizes sections and task lines, but does NOT extract dates, types, durations, or dependencies
- Layout has a gantt algorithm but operates on generic nodes, not time-aware bars

## Implementation Plan
1. **Parser**: After the colon in task lines, parse comma-separated metadata: type (done/active/crit/milestone), id, start (date or 'after id'), end (date or duration). Parse dateFormat directive. Parse excludes.
2. **IR**: Add IrGanttMeta { date_format, excludes, sections: Vec<IrGanttSection> } with IrGanttTask { id, name, task_type, start, end, depends_on }.
3. **Layout**: Compute actual x-positions from dates. Apply excludes to skip weekends. Position milestone as diamonds.
4. **Tests**: Date formats, durations, after-dependencies, excludes, milestones, crit tasks.
close_reason: Already implemented: gantt parser extracts dateFormat, excludes (weekends + dates), tick_interval, sections, task types (done/active/crit/milestone), task IDs, start dates (absolute + after-dependency), end dates (absolute + duration), and progress values. IrGanttMeta fully populated. 9 existing tests verify all features. Marking as complete since the gap described in the bead has been closed by prior work.

title: State transition labels corrupt edges and nodes in realistic docs corpus
description: Full ci_docs_2000/5000 equivalence at 905b01f9 proves 105/169 and 227/390 state diagrams divergent. The failures are exactly diagrams containing one of five label forms. In parse_state_statements, the generic edge endpoint parser sees the colon-suffix label before state-specific extraction: top-level ampersands in Retry & backoff, Diff & merge, or Sign & upload are rejected as parallel endpoint lists, recovery then creates a phantom asymmetric node and drops each affected transition; Parse <config> is misread as an asymmetric-node delimiter; Rate limit (429) is misread as a rounded-node delimiter. The last two preserve edge count but lose visible label tokens. Fix the state grammar so colon suffixes remain transition labels and never endpoint syntax. Add focused parse/render tests for all five labels, exact node/edge/label assertions, and require zero state divergences/unverified in fresh full ci_docs_2000 and ci_docs_5000 linked equivalence artifacts.
notes:
FIX IMPLEMENTED AND FUNCTIONALLY VERIFIED (cc lane, LilacPike) — not yet committed.

split_state_transition_label() peels the ': label' suffix off before the generic flowchart edge
parser sees it, and the label is attached to FlowAst::Edge's existing label field.

Three deliberate design points:
- Only splits AFTER an edge operator, so a bare 'S1: description' (mermaid's state-description
  syntax, which sets the state's own label) still flows to the node parser untouched.
- label.or_else(...) not Some(...), so an explicit '-->|text|' keeps its own label instead of being
  overwritten by the colon suffix.
- Structural scan mirroring find_operator_core (quotes + [] () {} depth), not split_once(':'), so
  '[*]' and parenthesised text do not confuse it and the FIRST top-level colon wins, matching mermaid
  on 'S0 --> S1: Rate: 429'.

TEST RESULT at base 77c3a091 with the overlay, --no-fail-fast so nothing was masked:
  integration_test: 121 passed; 0 failed

THREE GOLDEN-DERIVED SUITES FAIL with the overlay:

  layout_golden_checksums_are_stable
  differential_all_golden_cases_pass_gate
The first two are EXPECTED and require re-blessing: state_basic.svg and state_composite.svg encode
the bug (they render 'Idle : stop' / 'Running : start' as NODE labels with no edge labels at all), and

title: Edge routing: clip edges at node boundaries via CGA intersection (bd-2q3f.3 criterion 2)
description:
bd-2q3f.3 criterion 2: 'Edge routing uses CGA intersection for node boundary clipping'. Split out of bd-2q3f.3 because, unlike criteria 1/3/4 which were satisfiable in fm-core alone, this one CHANGES EMITTED GEOMETRY and therefore cannot ride along on a test-only change.

SCOPE: fm-layout edge routing currently clips edge endpoints at node boundaries with its own arithmetic. Replacing that with CgaRect::intersect_segment / CgaLineSegment::intersect would route every edge endpoint through fm-core's CGA primitives.

WHY THIS IS NOT A FREE SWAP:
- Edge endpoint coordinates appear directly in rendered SVG path data, so ANY numeric difference moves goldens. This requires a GOLDEN-CHANGE note plus a semantic diff review per AGENTS.md, never a bulk refresh.
- The CGA primitives fail closed to CgaPoint::origin() on malformed input. An edge silently clipped to (0,0) would be a visible corruption, not a diagnostic. Any adoption must distinguish 'no intersection' from 'rejected input' at the call site -- note bd-34yo was exactly this ambiguity biting inside fm-core.
- CgaRect::intersect_segment dedupes corner hits with an absolute f64::EPSILON comparison, which is magnitude-blind; check it against real layout coordinate ranges before relying on it.

PRE-SPECIFIED ASSERTIONS (code and tests in the SAME bead):
- POSITIVE: an edge between two separated nodes is clipped exactly at the boundary of each -- endpoint lies on the node rect within tolerance, and outside the node interior.
- NEGATIVE CASE a naive implementation fails: overlapping / nested node rects, and an edge whose endpoints are both INSIDE the source node. A naive 'take the first intersection' returns nothing or the wrong side; assert the documented behaviour rather than whatever falls out.
- NEGATIVE CASE: zero-size and degenerate (zero-width or zero-height) node rects must not produce origin-clipped edges.
- Determinism: repeated layout of the same input yields byte-identical paths.

GOLDEN HANDLING: expect movement. Every changed golden needs its delta explained semantically (which edge, which endpoint, by how much, and why the new value is the more correct clip). If a golden's geometry changes by more than a rounding-level amount, that is a finding to explain, not to bless.

DEPENDS ON bd-9mqa: if that decides the analytic queries are the intended endpoint, this bead's framing changes from 'adopt CGA meet' to 'consolidate duplicated clipping arithmetic onto the shared fm-core primitives' -- same code, different justification, and the perf criterion (bd-2q3f.3 criterion 5) then has to price a real abstraction boundary.
close_reason:
REFUTED on inspection — both readings of this bead fail, so no code was changed. I filed this bead; closing my own.

READING 1, 'adopt CGA intersection for boundary clipping': dead on arrival. There is no meet()/join(), and bd-9mqa (closed, with measurement) shows CGA machinery costs 10-40x the direct arithmetic it would replace.

READING 2, the reframing I gave it after bd-9mqa — 'consolidate duplicated clipping arithmetic onto the shared fm-core primitives': THERE IS NO DUPLICATION. Verified by grep across crates/: clip_to_rect_border has exactly one definition (lib.rs:9013) and exactly two call sites (lib.rs:8995, 8996, the two endpoints of one edge). cga_routing.rs does use CgaRect::intersect_segment already, but for a DIFFERENT job — testing whether a segment hits an expanded obstacle rect during routing — not for clipping an endpoint to a node border. The premise that two implementations had drifted apart is simply false.

AND THE SWAP WOULD REGRESS. clip_to_rect_border is a ~10-flop f32 ray-vs-centered-rect clip: center, direction, t = min(half_w/|dx|, half_h/|dy|), return center + t*d. CgaRect::intersect_segment would replace that, per edge endpoint, with: constructing an f64 rect and segment, iterating all four edges with a full segment-segment intersection each, an O(k^2) corner dedup, and a heap-allocated Vec<CgaPoint> RETURN — an allocation per endpoint in the layout hot path, twice per edge. It would also change emitted geometry (f32 -> f64 and a different formula), moving goldens to pay for a slowdown.

Existing implementation audited while here and is correct:  is always the node centre at both call sites so the centre-projection is consistent; zero-size rect yields t=0 and returns the centre; a degenerate direction returns . No latent defect found to justify touching it.

UNVERIFIED OBSERVATION, deliberately NOT acted on and NOT filed as fact: clip_to_rect_border always clips to the bounding RECT, so for non-rectangular shapes (circle, diamond, stadium) an edge may meet the bounding box rather than the drawn outline. Whether that is visible depends on what the renderers do at their end, which I did not check. If someone is working cross-engine visual fidelity, that is worth confirming — but it is a shape-aware-clipping question, not a CGA-adoption one, and it should not be smuggled back into bd-2q3f.

Consequence for the parent: bd-2q3f.3 criterion 2 ('edge routing uses CGA intersection for node boundary clipping') should be struck rather than implemented, on the same evidence as criteria 1-3 being reworded per bd-9mqa. Implementing it as literally written would knowingly make the engine slower and its output different for no benefit.

comments.author: PeachGorge
comments.text:
UNBLOCKED — bd-9mqa is decided (option b, closed). Its dependency is satisfied and its framing collapses to the second of the two alternatives this bead names.

This bead is NOT 'adopt CGA meet for boundary clipping'. There is no meet() to adopt, and the measurement on bd-9mqa shows CGA transforms cost 10-40x the matrices they would replace while the one load-bearing use of conformal machinery (distance) was numerically wrong and had to be replaced (681cdf4a). So the work is: CONSOLIDATE the duplicated edge/node clipping arithmetic onto the shared fm-core primitives that already exist (CgaRect::intersect_segment, CgaLineSegment::intersect), for single-implementation and correctness reasons — not for an algebraic abstraction.

Everything else in the bead stands unchanged, and the warnings in it matter more under this framing, not less: it still changes emitted geometry, so it still needs a GOLDEN-CHANGE note with a semantic diff, and it still must distinguish a fail-closed origin result from 'no intersection' or an edge silently clips to (0,0).

title: Eliminate Rayon stealing from production batch scheduling
description: Post-ba916fc5 whole-job profile ranks frankenmermaid-only Rayon coordination at 17.50% queued spinlock, 5.27% epoch pin, 1.50% collection, and 1.24% stealing. Replace dynamic work stealing with deterministic contiguous shared-nothing ranges while preserving 64-core execution and exact output order.
close_reason: Rejected and fully reverted: same-binary fixed contiguous shards cut 62.3% cycles but lost whole-job median by 1.97%; round-robin and a second static load cohort regressed further.

title: REJECT (inconclusive): BK rank_pos_maps -> flat node_position Vec
description: frankenmermaid-cc: replaced brandes_kopf_secondary_coords' rank_pos_maps (BTreeMap<rank,BTreeMap<node,pos>>, R per-rank heap allocs, O(log) lookups) with a flat node_position: Vec<usize> (1 alloc, O(1) lookups). Output-identical (428 fm-layout tests pass single-threaded; node's position is global since each node is in one rank). BUT measurement inconclusive: same-worker A/B gave contradictory results across runs (cyclic_50 +35% then -10.5%; medium_100 consistently OPT-slower -4.5% to -20%). Root cause: stash-swap A/B has a WARM-UP BIAS (OPT always runs first, ORIG second runs systematically faster), which swamps small effects. Mechanically the flat Vec helps only WIDE/multi-node-rank graphs (lookups on multi-entry maps); for CHAINS (1 node/rank) the BTreeMaps are 1-entry so lookups don't improve -> net ~0. Cannot confirm >=3% on the common case. REVERTED (stashed, not dropped). LESSON: stash-swap A/B order bias favors the second (ORIG) run; for small effects, run a REVERSE-ORDER A/B (orig first) to detect order-dependence before trusting.
close_reason: Reverted ~0/inconclusive; warm-up bias swamps the small effect; chains see no lookup gain

title: Sequence: support named box colors and transparent box syntax parity
description:
# Sequence box color parity

## Goal
Support Mermaid sequence box declarations that use named colors and the special transparent form, matching current docs examples like `box Aqua Group Description` and `box transparent Aqua`.

## Scope
- Parse leading named CSS color tokens in sequence `box` declarations, not just hex/rgb/hsl forms.
- Treat `box transparent <label>` as transparent box fill with `<label>` preserved as the label.
- Preserve the parsed group color through sequence IR/layout to SVG rendering for participant group clusters.
- Add focused parser/layout/render tests.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `box Aqua Group` stores color `Aqua` and label `Group`.
- `box transparent Aqua` stores a transparent color and label `Aqua`.
- SVG uses the parsed group color without unsafe attribute injection.
- Quality gates for touched crates pass via `rch` and formatting is clean.
close_reason: Implemented sequence box color parity

title: Implement composite/nested states with containment and concurrency
description:
# Composite/Nested States and Concurrency

## What mermaid-js Supports
\`\`\`
stateDiagram-v2
  state Active {
    [*] --> Processing
    Processing --> Done
    --
    [*] --> Monitoring
    Monitoring --> Alert
  }
  Idle --> Active
  Active --> Idle
\`\`\`
- States can contain child states (composite state)
- \`--\` separator creates concurrent regions within a composite state
- Each concurrent region has independent start/end states
- Nesting can be arbitrarily deep

## Current State
- Composite state syntax (\`state Name { ... }\`) IS parsed — creates subgraphs
- Concurrency separator \`--\` is NOT parsed
- Layout does not enforce visual containment of child states
- SVG renderer draws clusters but doesn't render concurrency dividers

## Implementation Plan
1. **Parser**: Parse \`--\` within composite state blocks as region separators. Each region becomes a separate sub-cluster within the parent cluster.
2. **Layout**: Ensure cluster bounds fully contain all child node bounds. For concurrent regions, split the cluster horizontally with a dashed divider.
3. **SVG Renderer**: Draw composite states with rounded rectangle borders. Draw dashed horizontal line for concurrency dividers. Add region labels if present.
4. **Tests**: Nested states, three levels deep, concurrent regions, transitions crossing region boundaries.
close_reason: Completed
